questions.q: What was the theme of the 18th BRICS Summit held in New Delhi on 12-13 September 2026 under India's chairship?
options: Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability
Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security
Strengthening Global South Cooperation for a More Inclusive and Sustainable Governance
BRICS and Africa: Partnership for Mutually Accelerated Growth
questions.explanation: The theme was 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'. The summit was held in New Delhi on 12-13 September 2026, adopted the New Delhi Declaration and was India's 4th BRICS chairship (after 2012, 2016 and 2021). China chairs BRICS in 2027. Source: SAnews (South African Government), 13 Sep 2026.

questions.q: The 26th meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of State, which marked 25 years of the organisation, was held on 1 September 2026 in which city?
questions.explanation: The summit was held on 1 September 2026 at the Yrys-Ordo Congress Hall in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, and was chaired by President Sadyr Japarov. Pakistan took over the chair for 2026-27, and Lahore was named SCO Tourism and Cultural Capital for 2026-27. Source: SCO Secretariat, 1 Sep 2026.

questions.q: The 52nd G7 Summit, which Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended in June 2026, was held at which place?
questions.explanation: France hosted the 52nd G7 Summit at Evian-les-Bains on 15-17 June 2026 under President Emmanuel Macron. India attended as an invited partner country. The 2025 summit was at Kananaskis, Canada. Source: Elysee (French Presidency), 17 Jun 2026.

questions.q: On which date did the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) come into force?
questions.explanation: CETA came into force on 15 July 2026. It was signed on 24 July 2025 and gives duty-free access to about 99% of India's exports to the UK (by tariff lines). Source: GOV.UK, Jul 2026.

questions.q: COP31, the UN climate conference of November 2026, is being held in which city?
questions.explanation: COP31 is being held in Antalya, Turkiye, from 9 to 20 November 2026. Turkiye holds the presidency and Australia leads the negotiations. COP30 was held in Belem, Brazil. Source: UNFCCC, Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which city hosted the Annual Meetings of the IMF and the World Bank Group in October 2026?
questions.explanation: The 2026 Annual Meetings were held in Bangkok, Thailand, on 12-18 October 2026. Thailand last hosted them in 1991. Both the IMF and the World Bank are headquartered in Washington, D.C. Source: IMF, Oct 2026.

questions.q: The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, signed in April 2026, came into force on which date?
questions.explanation: The India-New Zealand FTA came into force on 20 October 2026, after both countries ratified it. It was signed on 27 April 2026 and gives 100% of India's exports duty-free access to New Zealand. New Zealand has committed to facilitate USD 20 billion of investment in India over 15 years. Source: MFAT (New Zealand), Oct 2026; IBEF, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Uzbekistan became the 10th member of the New Development Bank (NDB) in June 2026. In which city is the NDB headquartered?
questions.explanation: The NDB, set up by the BRICS countries, is headquartered in Shanghai, China. Uzbekistan joined on 5 June 2026, the first Central Asian member, after Bangladesh, UAE, Egypt and Algeria. Its President is Dilma Rousseff. Source: New Development Bank, Jun 2026.

questions.q: The Asian Development Bank (ADB), in which Japan and the United States are the largest shareholders, has its headquarters in which city?
questions.explanation: ADB is headquartered in Manila, Philippines, and was set up in 1966. Japan and the US are its largest shareholders, and India is a founding member. Source: ADB website.

questions.q: In October 2026, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the sale of a majority stake in IDBI Bank to a subsidiary of which group?
questions.explanation: On 14 October 2026 the CCEA cleared the sale to 10955230 Canada Inc., a subsidiary of Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings, for about Rs 52,878 crore (Rs 81 a share). The Government and LIC are the sellers, and the deal needs RBI approval to close. IDBI Bank is headquartered in Mumbai. Source: Business Today, 14 Oct 2026.

questions.q: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026 raised the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court, including the Chief Justice of India, from 34 to what number?
questions.explanation: The Act raised the number of judges other than the CJI from 33 to 37, so the total is 38. It replaced an Ordinance of 16 May 2026 and amends the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956. Source: LiveLaw, 12 Aug 2026; PRS Session Wrap, Monsoon Session 2026.

questions.q: The Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, 2026, passed in the Monsoon Session, made it an offence to deliberately disrupt the singing of which of the following?
questions.explanation: The amendment extends the 1971 Act's protection from the National Anthem to the National Song, Vande Mataram, written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay. The penalty is up to three years' imprisonment, or fine, or both. Source: PRS Session Wrap, Monsoon Session 2026; SCC Online, 21 Aug 2026.

questions.q: In October 2026 the Finance Ministry set up a High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat. Who chairs it?
questions.explanation: Former Central Vigilance Commissioner Suresh N. Patel chairs the committee, which the Finance Ministry set up on 30 October 2026 with six months (until April 2027) to report. It was announced in the Union Budget 2026-27. It will recommend structural, regulatory and legislative changes, including a review of priority sector lending and the Lead Bank Scheme. Source: Free Press Journal, 31 Oct 2026.

questions.q: After India's chairship in 2026, which country will chair BRICS and host the 19th BRICS Summit in 2027?
questions.explanation: The New Delhi Declaration of September 2026 supported China's BRICS chairship in 2027. Brazil chaired in 2025 (Rio de Janeiro) and Russia in 2024 (Kazan). Source: SAnews (South African Government), 13 Sep 2026.

questions.q: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), which marked 25 years in 2026, has its secretariat in which city?
questions.explanation: The SCO Secretariat is in Beijing; its Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) is in Tashkent. The SCO was founded in 2001 and has 10 members. Pakistan chairs it in 2026-27. Source: SCO Secretariat, 1 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which country hosted the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) in November 2026?
questions.explanation: CHOGM 2026 was held in St John's, Antigua and Barbuda, on 1-4 November 2026 on the theme 'Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth'. Samoa hosted in 2024 and Rwanda in 2022. Source: Commonwealth Secretariat, Nov 2026.

questions.q: How many member countries does the Commonwealth of Nations, whose leaders met at CHOGM 2026, have?
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth has 56 member countries; Gabon and Togo were the latest to join, in 2022. Its secretariat is at Marlborough House, London, and King Charles III is its Head. Source: Commonwealth Secretariat, Nov 2026.

questions.q: The NATO Summit of 7-8 July 2026 was held in which city?
questions.explanation: The 2026 NATO Summit was held in Ankara, Turkiye, on 7-8 July 2026 and ended with a summit declaration. The 2025 summit was in The Hague and the 2024 summit in Washington, D.C. Source: Al Jazeera, 8 Jul 2026.

questions.q: NATO, which held its 2026 summit in July, has its headquarters in which city?
questions.explanation: NATO is headquartered in Brussels, Belgium. It was founded in 1949 by the Washington Treaty and has 32 members; Sweden was the latest to join, in 2024. Source: NATO; Al Jazeera, 8 Jul 2026.

questions.q: President Droupadi Murmu's State Visits of 19-25 July 2026 covered Moldova, North Macedonia and which third country?
questions.explanation: The President visited Moldova, North Macedonia and Romania. It was the first visit by an Indian President to Moldova and to North Macedonia. Romania's capital is Bucharest. Source: Akashvani News (newsonair), 26 Jul 2026.

questions.q: During Prime Minister Modi's State Visit of 29-30 August 2026, India raised its ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with which Central Asian country?
questions.explanation: The PM paid a State Visit to Tashkent at the invitation of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, and the two sides raised ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. Uzbekistan agreed to set up a framework for long-term uranium supply to India. He then went to Bishkek for the SCO summit. Source: News On AIR, 30-31 Aug 2026.

questions.q: In July 2026 the World Bank approved about USD 890 million of financing for which Government of India scheme?
options: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
questions.explanation: The package has a USD 820 million IBRD loan, a USD 60 million Clean Technology Fund loan and a USD 10 million Livable Planet Fund grant, and aims to mobilise about USD 4.2 billion of private finance. The rooftop solar scheme targets 10 million households. Source: World Bank press release, 9 Jul 2026.

questions.q: India's Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) with which Gulf country came into force on 1 June 2026?
questions.explanation: The India-Oman CEPA was signed in Muscat on 18 December 2025 and came into force on 1 June 2026. Oman's currency is the Omani rial. India's CEPA with the UAE has been in force since 2022. Source: India Briefing FTA tracker, 2026.

questions.q: The 48th session of the UNESCO World Heritage Committee, which inscribed Sarnath on the World Heritage List in July 2026, was held in which city?
questions.explanation: The session was held in Busan, South Korea, on 19-29 July 2026, and Sarnath's inscription was announced on 25 July 2026. The 46th session was in New Delhi (2024) and the 47th in Paris (2025). UNESCO is headquartered in Paris. Source: UNESCO; News On AIR, 25 Jul 2026.

questions.q: Which country holds the presidency of the G20 in 2026?
questions.explanation: The United States holds the G20 presidency in 2026 and hosts the leaders' summit at Doral, Miami, in December 2026. South Africa held the presidency in 2025 (Johannesburg summit) and India in 2023. Source: G20 / White House, 2026.

questions.q: Which country will host COP32, the UN climate change conference, in 2027?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia will host COP32 in Addis Ababa in 2027. It won the African Group's backing over Nigeria, and the choice was announced at COP30 in Belem, Brazil, in November 2025. COP31 is being held in Antalya, Turkiye (9-20 November 2026), with Australia leading the negotiations. The UNFCCC secretariat is in Bonn, Germany. Source: Reuters via The Star, 11 Nov 2025; UNFCCC, Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a member of the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), with which India held the 2nd Prosperity Summit in October 2026?
questions.explanation: EFTA has four members: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. The India-EFTA TEPA came into force on 1 October 2025, with a pledge of USD 100 billion investment in 15 years. Source: AffairsCloud, 13 Oct 2026; IANS, 7 Oct 2026.

questions.q: The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB), which approved a USD 1 billion loan to India in July 2026, has its headquarters in which city?
questions.explanation: AIIB is headquartered in Beijing, China, and began operations in 2016. On 16 July 2026 it approved USD 1 billion for India's Program for Growth, Resilience, Energy Security and Sustainability. India is its second-largest shareholder. Source: AIIB, Jul 2026.

questions.q: What percentage stake in IDBI Bank, held jointly by the Government of India and LIC, was approved for sale in October 2026?
questions.explanation: The stake of 60.72% is made up of 30.48% from the Government and 30.24% from LIC, for Rs 52,878 crore. After the sale the Government keeps 15% and LIC 19%. Source: PRS Monthly Policy Review, October 2026; Outlook Business, 14 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Kerala was renamed 'Keralam' by the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026. Which Article of the Constitution empowers Parliament to alter the name of a State?
questions.explanation: Article 3 allows Parliament to form new States and alter the areas, boundaries or names of existing States. The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill was passed by the Lok Sabha on 11 August and the Rajya Sabha on 12 August 2026, received Presidential assent in August, and came into force on 25 August 2026; it changes the name in the First Schedule. Source: Onmanorama, 18 and 26 Aug 2026.

questions.q: In November 2026, State Bank of India secured a social loan from the International Finance Corporation (IFC) to finance about 8.64 lakh rural women. What was the loan amount?
questions.explanation: The USD 150 million loan mainly reaches women through Self-Help Groups. It is IFC's first line of credit to a public sector bank in India. IFC is the private-sector arm of the World Bank Group, based in Washington DC. Source: PTI via The Week, 6 Nov 2026.

questions.q: The Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, known as VB-G RAM G, came into force on 1 July 2026. Which law did it replace?
options: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005
questions.explanation: VB-G RAM G replaced MGNREGA, 2005 from 1 July 2026; the Ministry of Rural Development notified the commencement date on 11 May 2026, and MGNREGA stands repealed. It raises the guaranteed wage employment from 100 to 125 days per rural household in a financial year. Source: SCC Online, 12 May 2026; PRS Monthly Policy Review, July 2026.

questions.q: Who heads the 8th Central Pay Commission, whose report was still awaited in 2026?
questions.explanation: Former Supreme Court judge Ranjana Prakash Desai chairs the 8th Pay Commission, set up by a resolution of 3 November 2025 with 18 months to report. Justice A. K. Mathur headed the 7th and Justice B. N. Srikrishna the 6th. Source: The Hans India, 2026.

questions.q: Commercial flights at Noida International Airport, Jewar, began on 15 June 2026. Which airline operated the first flight?
questions.explanation: An IndiGo flight from Lucknow was the first to land. Akasa Air started the next day. The airport is in Gautam Buddh Nagar district, Uttar Pradesh, and was inaugurated by the Prime Minister on 28 March 2026. Source: All India Radio News, 15 Jun 2026.

questions.q: Which defence shipbuilder was granted Navratna status in June 2026, becoming India's 29th Navratna CPSE?
questions.explanation: GRSE, based in Kolkata under the Ministry of Defence, was upgraded on 19 June 2026. Chennai Petroleum Corporation became the 28th Navratna the same day. A Navratna can invest up to Rs 1,000 crore in a project without government approval. Source: Indian Mandarins, 22 Jun 2026.

questions.q: The Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 2026, in force from 1 October 2026, replaced an Act of which year?
questions.explanation: It replaced the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891 and recognises electronic and digital bank records as evidence. Presidential assent came on 13 August 2026. Source: PRS Session Wrap, Monsoon Session 2026; SCC Online, 21 Aug 2026.

questions.q: The MSME Development (Amendment) Act, 2026 makes central PSUs settle MSME invoices on TReDS. What does TReDS stand for?
questions.explanation: TReDS is the Trade Receivables Discounting System, an RBI-authorised platform where MSME invoices are discounted. The MSMED (Amendment) Act, 2026, which received assent on 13 August 2026, requires every Central Public Sector Enterprise to settle MSME invoices through TReDS and tightens timelines for settling delayed-payment disputes. Source: SCC Online, 19 Aug 2026; PRS Monthly Policy Review, August 2026.

questions.q: The Bill for simultaneous elections ('One Nation, One Election'), still before a Joint Parliamentary Committee in 2026, is which Constitution Amendment Bill?
questions.explanation: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 provides for simultaneous Lok Sabha and Assembly elections; the JPC is chaired by P. P. Chaudhary. The 130th Amendment Bill, 2025 deals with removal of ministers held in detention. Source: PRS Session Wrap, Monsoon Session 2026.

questions.q: Sarnath, inscribed in July 2026 as India's 45th UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Sarnath, near Varanasi in Uttar Pradesh, is where the Buddha gave his first sermon. It was inscribed on 25 July 2026 at the World Heritage Committee session in Busan, South Korea. Source: Wikipedia, 2026 in India, 25 Jul 2026.

questions.q: What is the theme of the general debate of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, held in September 2026?
options: Rebuilding trust and reigniting global solidarity
Better together: 80 years and more for peace, development and human rights
Leaving no one behind: acting together for peace, sustainable development and human dignity
Restoring trust, managing transformation: a United Nations that delivers for all
questions.explanation: The theme of the 81st session is 'Restoring trust, managing transformation: a United Nations that delivers for all'. Its general debate opened on 22 September 2026 at UN Headquarters in New York. The 80th session's theme was 'Better together: 80 years and more for peace, development and human rights'. The UN has 193 member states. Source: United Nations, High-level week 2026, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Under the bilateral Haj Agreement signed with Saudi Arabia in Jeddah in November 2026, what is India's pilgrim quota for Haj 2027?
questions.explanation: Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju signed the bilateral Haj Agreement for 2027 with Saudi Hajj and Umrah Minister Tawfiq Al-Rabiah in Jeddah on 9 November 2026. India's quota stays at 1,75,025 pilgrims. Source: News On AIR, 10 Nov 2026; GKToday, 10 Nov 2026.

questions.q: SBI Funds Management Ltd, which listed on the stock exchanges on 21 July 2026, is a joint venture between State Bank of India and which French asset manager?
questions.explanation: SBI Funds Management, which runs SBI Mutual Fund, is a joint venture of SBI and Amundi of France. Its IPO of about Rs 9,813 crore was entirely an offer for sale at Rs 574 a share. Source: Groww, 21 Jul 2026.

questions.q: What is the reference date for Census 2027, India's first digital census, for most of the country?
questions.explanation: The reference date is 00:00 hours of 1 March 2027; for snow-bound areas it is 1 October 2026. Population enumeration is scheduled for February 2027 under the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, Ministry of Home Affairs. Source: MHA notification, Jun 2025; Adda247, 31 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Emirates NBD acquired a 60% stake in which Indian private sector bank in June 2026?
questions.explanation: Emirates NBD of Dubai completed the purchase of 60% of RBL Bank in June 2026 through a preferential issue. RBI later approved merging Emirates NBD's Indian branches into RBL Bank. RBL Bank is headquartered in Mumbai. Source: AffairsCloud, 19 Oct 2026; Adda247, 17 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Sankoo, carved out of Kargil in October 2026, became the 8th district of which Union Territory?
questions.explanation: Ladakh's Lieutenant Governor announced Sankoo as the 8th district on 16 October 2026, with its own Hill Development Council. Ladakh became a Union Territory on 31 October 2019. Source: AffairsCloud, 19 Oct 2026; Wikipedia, Ladakh.

questions.q: Guy Parmelin, who paid a State Visit to India on 5-7 October 2026, is the President of which country?
questions.explanation: Swiss President Guy Parmelin met PM Modi at Hyderabad House and attended the 2nd India-EFTA Prosperity Summit in New Delhi. Switzerland's capital is Bern and its currency is the Swiss franc. Source: IANS (Morung Express), 7 Oct 2026.

questions.q: In June 2026 Prime Minister Modi was Guest of Honour at the Golden Jubilee National Day celebrations of which island country?
questions.explanation: The PM paid a State Visit to Seychelles on 27-29 June 2026 at the invitation of President Patrick Herminie. He was Guest of Honour at the celebrations marking 50 years of Seychelles' independence, the first Indian PM to receive this honour. The capital of Seychelles is Victoria. Source: News On AIR, 29 Jun 2026.

questions.q: During Prime Minister Modi's visit in July 2026, the last leg of a tour that also covered Indonesia and Australia, India raised its ties to a Strategic Partnership with which country?
questions.explanation: The PM met PM Christopher Luxon in Auckland on 11 July 2026. The two sides announced an India-New Zealand Strategic Partnership and aim to double bilateral trade by 2030. New Zealand's capital is Wellington. Source: News On AIR, 11-12 Jul 2026.

questions.q: Which country holds the chair of ASEAN in 2026 and hosted the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit?
questions.explanation: The Philippines chairs ASEAN in 2026 and hosted the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and 21st East Asia Summit in Manila on 17 November 2026. Malaysia chaired in 2025. The ASEAN Secretariat is in Jakarta. Source: Akashvani News, 17 Nov 2026.

questions.q: The UN General Assembly has declared 2027 as the International Year of what?
questions.explanation: 2027 is the International Year of Sustainable and Resilient Tourism, declared by a resolution adopted on 26 February 2024; UN Tourism will coordinate it. Glaciers' Preservation and Quantum Science were themes for 2025. Source: FAO Mountain Partnership / UN Tourism.

questions.q: On 20 July 2026 India became the 123rd member to accept which World Trade Organization agreement?
questions.explanation: India deposited its instrument of acceptance for the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies on 20 July 2026. The agreement was adopted at MC12 in Geneva in 2022 and came into force on 15 September 2025. The WTO is headquartered in Geneva. Source: WTO, Jul 2026.

questions.q: Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd, which became India's 28th Navratna CPSE in June 2026, is a subsidiary of which company?
questions.explanation: CPCL is a subsidiary of Indian Oil Corporation under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. It was upgraded from Miniratna Category-I on 19 June 2026. Source: Indian Mandarins, 22 Jun 2026.

questions.q: The Tribunals Reforms Act, 2026 creates which new body to handle appointments to tribunals and review their performance?
questions.explanation: The National Tribunals Commission is chaired by a former Supreme Court judge or High Court Chief Justice. The Act repeals the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021 and received assent on 13 August 2026. Source: PRS Monthly Policy Review, August 2026.

questions.q: The Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026, notified by the Ministry of Civil Aviation and effective from 1 January 2027, replace which rules?
questions.explanation: The new rules are framed under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024 and replace the Aircraft Rules, 1937. The DGCA is the civil aviation regulator. Source: PRS Monthly Policy Review, October 2026.

questions.q: The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026 amends the parent Act of which year?
questions.explanation: It amends the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. A registration delayed beyond two years now needs an order of a Judicial Magistrate First Class. Source: SCC Online, 21 Aug 2026; PRS Session Wrap, Monsoon Session 2026.

questions.q: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance of May 2026 was promulgated by the President under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 123 lets the President promulgate Ordinances when Parliament is not in session; Article 213 gives the same power to Governors. Parliament replaced the Ordinance with an Act in August 2026. Source: SCC Online, 2026.

questions.q: Who took charge as Managing Director and CEO of HDFC Bank on 27 October 2026?
questions.explanation: Anup Bagchi took charge on 27 October 2026 after RBI approved a three-year term. He succeeded Sashidhar Jagdishan, whose tenure ended on 26 October 2026, and came from ICICI Prudential Life Insurance. Source: Business Today, 27 Oct 2026.

questions.q: In October 2026, the RBI approved whom as MD and CEO of Kotak Mahindra Bank for three years from 1 January 2027?
questions.explanation: RBI approved Anup Kumar Saha, a whole-time director of the bank and former Bajaj Finance executive, for three years from 1 January 2027. He will succeed Ashok Vaswani, whose term ends on 31 December 2026. Source: ThePrint (Bloomberg), 1 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Who took over as the Chief of the Army Staff on 30 June 2026, succeeding General Upendra Dwivedi?
questions.explanation: General Dhiraj Seth, an Armoured Corps officer commissioned in December 1986, took over on 30 June 2026. He is the first Armoured Corps officer to head the Army since 1997, and his tenure runs to August 2028. Source: Free Press Journal (IANS), 30 Jun 2026.

questions.q: Who took charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff on 31 October 2026?
questions.explanation: Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit took charge on 31 October 2026, succeeding Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh, who retired after 42 years of service. Dixit was earlier Vice Chief of the Air Staff and was commissioned in the fighter stream in 1986. Source: All India Radio News, 31 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Who became the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom on 20 July 2026 after Keir Starmer resigned?
questions.explanation: Andy Burnham became Prime Minister on 20 July 2026 after Keir Starmer resigned; he had been elected Leader of the Labour Party on 16 July 2026. He was earlier Mayor of Greater Manchester and returned to Parliament by winning the Makerfield by-election in June 2026. Source: GOV.UK, 20 Jul 2026.

questions.q: Who was sworn in as Chief Minister of Karnataka on 3 June 2026?
questions.explanation: Congress leader D.K. Shivakumar was sworn in on 3 June 2026 by Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot, succeeding Siddaramaiah, who resigned on 28 May 2026. Shivakumar had been elected leader of the Congress Legislature Party on 30 May 2026, and G. Parameshwara took oath as Deputy Chief Minister. Source: All India Radio News, 3 Jun 2026.

questions.q: Mahesh Muralidhar Pai, earlier a Chief General Manager at Canara Bank, became MD and CEO of which private sector bank from 1 October 2026?
questions.explanation: RBI approved Pai as MD & CEO of South Indian Bank for three years from 1 October 2026; he succeeded P.R. Seshadri. The bank is headquartered in Thrissur, Kerala. Source: Business Standard, 8 Jul 2026.

questions.q: Who was appointed Executive Director of the Reserve Bank of India with effect from 1 October 2026 to look after the Department of Supervision?
questions.explanation: RBI appointed Sudhakar Malli, earlier Chief General Manager-in-Charge of the Department of Supervision, as Executive Director from 1 October 2026. Other EDs appointed in 2026 include Ravi Shankar (1 July, Department of Statistics and Information Management), Monisha Chakraborty (3 August) and Suman Ray (1 September). Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/1241, 2 Oct 2026.

questions.q: In June 2026, the Centre re-appointed Swaminathan J as Deputy Governor of the RBI from 26 June 2026 for how long?
questions.explanation: Swaminathan J, a former SBI Managing Director, was re-appointed for two years from 26 June 2026. The RBI Act, 1934 provides for four Deputy Governors; the others are Poonam Gupta, S.C. Murmu and Rohit Jain. Source: RBI press release, 5 Jun 2026.

questions.q: Hitesh Rameshchandra Joshi was appointed Chairman-cum-Managing Director of which public sector company with effect from 16 June 2026?
options: General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC Re)
questions.explanation: Hitesh Joshi was appointed CMD of GIC Re, India's national reinsurer, from 16 June 2026 until 30 September 2028. He had been interim CMD since 1 October 2025. GIC Re is headquartered in Mumbai. Source: Reinsurance News, 17 Jun 2026.

questions.q: Who took charge as Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog in August 2026?
questions.explanation: Anurag Jain, a 1989-batch IAS officer of the Madhya Pradesh cadre, was appointed for two years in July 2026 and took charge on 17 August 2026. Nidhi Chhibber had held additional charge after B.V.R. Subrahmanyam's term ended. Source: Business Standard, 18 Aug 2026.

questions.q: S. Somanath, appointed a part-time non-official director on the RBI Central Board in August 2026, is a former chairman of which organisation?
questions.explanation: Former ISRO Chairman S. Somanath was appointed to the RBI Central Board for four years from 20 August 2026, and Anand Mahindra was re-appointed. Such directors are nominated under Section 8(1)(c) of the RBI Act, 1934. Source: AffairsCloud, 22 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Khalilur Rahman, who took office as President of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in September 2026, is from which country?
questions.explanation: Bangladesh's Khalilur Rahman took office on 8 September 2026, succeeding Germany's Annalena Baerbock (80th session). He was elected in June 2026, defeating Andreas Kakouris of Cyprus. Source: AffairsCloud, 4 Jun 2026.

questions.q: In the Governor appointments announced by the President on 12 October 2026, who was named Governor of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Former Lok Sabha MP Dr Sudha Yadav was named Governor of Karnataka, succeeding Thaawarchand Gehlot. The same order named Braj Mohan Ram for Odisha, Dhal Singh Bisen for Uttarakhand and Dushyant Gautam for Sikkim. Governors are appointed by the President under Article 155. Source: Organiser, 13 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Former Chief Election Commissioner Rajiv Kumar was approved by the RBI in July 2026 as part-time chairman of which bank?
questions.explanation: RBI approved Rajiv Kumar as part-time chairman of HDFC Bank for three years from 15 July 2026. He followed Atanu Chakraborty, who resigned in March 2026; Keki Mistry was interim chairman in between. Source: HDFC Bank filing, 15 Jul 2026.

questions.q: The UN Secretary-General, whose selection for the term starting 1 January 2027 was under way in November 2026, is appointed by the General Assembly on the recommendation of which body?
questions.explanation: Under Article 97 of the UN Charter, the General Assembly appoints the Secretary-General on the Security Council's recommendation. Antonio Guterres's term ends on 31 December 2026; no successor had been recommended by mid-November 2026. Source: Al Jazeera, 15 Nov 2026.

questions.q: In October 2026, who was appointed part-time Chairperson of the Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB) for three years?
questions.explanation: Retired IAS officer Subhash Chandra Lal (S.C.L.) Das was appointed FSIB Chairperson for three years from 16 October 2026. He succeeded Bhanu Pratap Sharma, whose extended tenure ended on 30 June 2026. FSIB recommends top appointments in public sector banks, financial institutions and insurers. Source: Indian Masterminds, 17 Oct 2026.

questions.q: After Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union Education Minister on 25 July 2026, which Union Minister was given additional charge of the Ministry of Education?
questions.explanation: Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on 25 July 2026 amid protests over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. On the Prime Minister's advice, the President assigned the Ministry of Education to Pralhad Joshi in addition to his existing portfolios of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and New and Renewable Energy. Joshi took charge at Kartavya Bhavan on 26 July 2026. Source: All India Radio News, 26 Jul 2026.

questions.q: In August 2026, the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet gave a one-year extension to which officer as Cabinet Secretary?
questions.explanation: T.V. Somanathan, Cabinet Secretary since August 2024, got a one-year extension and stays till 30 August 2027. Home Secretary Govind Mohan was also extended by a year to 22 August 2027. Source: Adda247, 6 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Who was elected President of the International Chess Federation (FIDE) on 26 September 2026?
questions.explanation: Kazakhstan's Timur Turlov was elected FIDE President at the General Assembly in Samarkand on 26 September 2026, replacing Arkady Dvorkovich, who had led FIDE since 2018. Turlov won a run-off against Wadim Rosenstein by 110 votes to 85. FIDE is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland. Source: Reuters, 26 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which Indian took over as interim President of FIDE in July 2026 after Arkady Dvorkovich suspended his duties?
questions.explanation: FIDE Deputy President Viswanathan Anand took charge as interim President on 24 July 2026 after Arkady Dvorkovich suspended his duties following EU sanctions. Anand is a five-time World Chess Champion. Timur Turlov was elected President on 26 September 2026, with Anand as Deputy President. Source: All India Radio News, 24 Jul 2026.

questions.q: In October 2026, the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet approved whom as the next Chairman of ONGC, to succeed Arun Kumar Singh in December 2026?
questions.explanation: ONGC Executive Director Sunil Kumar was approved on 21 October 2026 and takes charge on or after 7 December 2026; Arun Kumar Singh's extended tenure ends on 6 December 2026, so Singh is still chairman in November. ONGC is a Maharatna under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. Source: Adda247, 23 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Jatin Kumar Nayak took charge as CMD of IREDA at the end of October 2026. IREDA works under which ministry?
options: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
questions.explanation: IREDA (Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency) is a Navratna CPSE under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy. Jatin Kumar Nayak, earlier Executive Director (Finance) at REC, became its CMD on 30 October 2026. Source: Adda247, 31 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Monisha Chakraborty, appointed Executive Director of the RBI from 3 August 2026, was given charge of the Financial Markets Regulation Department and which other department?
options: Department of Statistics and Information Management
questions.explanation: Monisha Chakraborty, earlier Chief General Manager-in-Charge of the Department of Supervision, became Executive Director on 3 August 2026 with charge of the Foreign Exchange Department and the Financial Markets Regulation Department. RBI is headquartered in Mumbai. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/801, 3 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Suman Ray, who became an Executive Director of the RBI on 1 September 2026, was given charge of the Premises Department and the department dealing with which corporation?
options: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation
questions.explanation: Suman Ray, earlier RBI Regional Director for Maharashtra, became Executive Director from 1 September 2026 and was given charge of the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) department and the Premises Department. DICGC is a wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI that insures bank deposits. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/1013, 1 Sep 2026.

questions.q: In October 2026, Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar was moved from Keralam (Kerala) to be the Governor of which state?
questions.explanation: Arlekar was appointed full-time Governor of Tamil Nadu on 12 October 2026; he had held its additional charge since 12 March 2026. Om Prakash Mathur moved from Sikkim and was sworn in as Governor of Keralam in October 2026. Governors are appointed by the President under Article 155. Source: Organiser, 13 Oct 2026.

questions.q: In August 2026, renewable energy company Hero Future Energies named which sportsperson as its brand ambassador?
questions.explanation: Hero Future Energies, the renewable energy arm of the Hero Group, appointed badminton player P.V. Sindhu on 17 August 2026. Sindhu won Olympic silver in 2016 and bronze in 2020. Source: Manifest Media, 17 Aug 2026.

questions.q: In September 2026, which Nobel laureate was named Chief Economist of the World Bank Group?
questions.explanation: World Bank President Ajay Banga named Michael Kremer, joint winner of the 2019 Economics Nobel, as Chief Economist and Senior Vice President for Development Economics from 1 October 2026. The World Bank is headquartered in Washington, D.C. Source: World Bank press release, 16 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Jensen Huang resigned as President and CEO of which company on 12 November 2026?
questions.explanation: Jensen Huang, co-founder of Nvidia, resigned on 12 November 2026. CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones was named the first Chair of the Board. Source: NVIDIA Newsroom, 12 Nov 2026.

questions.q: Economist Neelkanth Mishra was approved in June 2026 as India's Executive Director at the World Bank. Whom does he succeed?
questions.explanation: The ACC approved Neelkanth Mishra, Chief Economist of Axis Bank, for three years; he succeeds Parameswaran Iyer. India's chair at the World Bank also represents Bangladesh, Bhutan and Sri Lanka. Source: AffairsCloud, 5 Jun 2026.

questions.q: Who won the run-off of Brazil's presidential election held on 25 October 2026?
questions.explanation: President Lula won a fourth term with about 51.8% of the vote against Flavio Bolsonaro, after trailing in the first round on 4 October 2026. Geraldo Alckmin is his Vice-President. Brazil's capital is Brasilia. Source: AffairsCloud, 27 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Who became the President of Bangladesh in August 2026 after Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned?
questions.explanation: BNP leader Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was elected by Parliament and has been President since 21 August 2026. Shahabuddin resigned on 24 July 2026 on health grounds. Tarique Rahman is the Prime Minister. Source: AffairsCloud, 22 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize 2026, announced in Oslo on 9 October 2026?
questions.explanation: South African jurist Navi Pillay won for promoting peace and international law. She was UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (2008-2014) and a judge of the International Criminal Court. Maria Corina Machado won in 2025. Source: AP, 12 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Which bank was named the 'World's Best Consumer Bank 2026' by Global Finance magazine in July 2026?
questions.explanation: Global Finance named SBI the World's Best Consumer Bank for 2026. Santander was named World's Best Bank and DBS the World's Best Corporate Bank. The awards were presented in Bangkok on 17 October 2026 during the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings. Source: Global Finance, 16 Jul 2026.

questions.q: The 2026 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences was awarded to which pair of economists?
options: Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford
questions.explanation: Robert E. Hall (Stanford) and Michael Woodford (Columbia), both American, won for the microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation. The prize was announced on 12 October 2026. Mokyr, Aghion and Howitt won in 2025. Source: AP, 12 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Who won the Booker Prize 2026, announced in London in November 2026, for the novel 'The End of Everything'?
questions.explanation: British writer M. John Harrison won on 9 November 2026. At 81 he is the oldest winner, and his is the first science fiction work to win. The prize money is 50,000 pounds; Mary Beard chaired the judges. Source: AP, 10 Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which film won the Best Feature Film award at the 72nd National Film Awards, presented by the President in September 2026?
questions.explanation: 'Article 370' won Best Feature Film. 'Kalki 2898 AD' won the popular film award, 'Srikanth' was Best Hindi Film, and Rajkumar Periasamy won Best Direction for 'Amaran'. The awards were announced on 18 July 2026 for films of 2024. Source: News On AIR, 22 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which veteran actor received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (for 2024) at the 72nd National Film Awards on 22 September 2026?
questions.explanation: Kannada actor Anant Nag received the award from President Droupadi Murmu. The award was first given in 1969 to Devika Rani. Mohanlal received the previous award (for 2023). Source: News On AIR, 22 Sep 2026.

questions.q: In the National Sports Awards 2025, announced on 18 August 2026, which award was not given to anyone?
questions.explanation: The Sports Ministry named no Khel Ratna awardee for 2025, the first such year since 2014. It named 17 Arjuna awardees, including Tejaswin Shankar and Divya Deshmukh. The President gave the awards on 13 November 2026. Source: PTI/ThePrint, 18 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Who won the Nobel Prize in Literature 2026?
questions.explanation: Canadian poet, essayist and translator Anne Carson, born in Toronto, won the prize announced on 8 October 2026. Laszlo Krasznahorkai won in 2025 and Han Kang in 2024. Source: AP, 12 Oct 2026.

questions.q: The Ramon Magsaysay Award, whose 2026 winners were announced on 31 August 2026, is named after a former President of which country?
questions.explanation: The award is named after Philippine President Ramon Magsaysay, who died in a plane crash in 1957. It was first given in 1958, is called Asia's Nobel Prize and is presented in Manila. Source: AP, 31 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Who among the following is one of the three winners of the Ramon Magsaysay Award 2026?
questions.explanation: The 2026 winners are Singapore diplomat Tommy Koh, Bangladeshi social worker Runa Khan and Myanmar activist Bo Kyi. Koh presided over the conference that adopted the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea in 1982. Source: AP, 31 Aug 2026.

questions.q: The prize in economic sciences in memory of Alfred Nobel, awarded in October 2026, was established in 1968 by which institution?
questions.explanation: Sweden's central bank, Sveriges Riksbank, set up the prize in 1968 for its 300th anniversary. It was first awarded in 1969. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences selects the winners. Source: Sveriges Riksbank.

questions.q: The 'Order of the White Double Cross (1st Class)', conferred on PM Narendra Modi in June 2026, is the highest state honour of which country?
questions.explanation: Slovak President Peter Pellegrini conferred the honour in Bratislava on 15 June 2026. It was reported as PM Modi's 33rd international honour. Source: IANS, 16 Jun 2026.

questions.q: In July 2026, PM Narendra Modi received Indonesia's highest civilian honour in Jakarta. What is it called?
options: Grand Collar of the Order of Timor-Leste
questions.explanation: President Prabowo Subianto conferred the Bintang Adipurna on 7 July 2026, reported as PM Modi's 35th international honour. The Order of the Druk Gyalpo is Bhutan's and the Order of Mubarak Al-Kabeer is Kuwait's. Source: PTI/OrissaPost, 7 Jul 2026.

questions.q: The 'Oliy Darajali Do'stlik' Order, conferred on PM Narendra Modi on 30 August 2026, is the highest honour for foreign leaders of which country?
questions.explanation: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev conferred it in Tashkent. PM Modi then went to Kyrgyzstan for the SCO summit. Source: PTI/Deccan Herald, 30 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Which bank was named 'India's Best Bank' in the Euromoney Awards for Excellence 2026?
questions.explanation: Euromoney named HDFC Bank India's best bank on 17 July 2026, citing 100 million customers and 9,616 branches. Santander was the world's best bank and HSBC was Asia's best bank. Source: Euromoney, 17 Jul 2026.

questions.q: Which film was selected in September 2026 as India's official entry for the 99th Academy Awards (Oscars 2027)?
questions.explanation: The Film Federation of India chose the Marathi film 'Gondhal', directed by Santosh Davakhar, from 33 films. It is the fourth Marathi entry after Shwaas, Harishchandrachi Factory and Court. 'Homebound' was the previous entry. Source: PTI/Onmanorama, 19 Sep 2026.

questions.q: How many gallantry awards did the President approve for armed forces and central police personnel on the eve of Independence Day 2026?
questions.explanation: President Murmu approved 78 gallantry awards on 14 August 2026, 13 of them posthumous. They include 9 Kirti Chakras and 19 Shaurya Chakras. The Kirti Chakra is the second-highest peacetime gallantry award after the Ashok Chakra. Source: PTI/ThePrint, 14 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Joheirry Mola, who was crowned Miss World 2026 in Vietnam on 5 September 2026, represents which country?
questions.explanation: She won the 73rd Miss World at Nha Trang, Vietnam, and was crowned by Opal Suchata Chuangsri of Thailand. Spain was first runner-up. India's Nikita Porwal reached the top 40. Source: Khaleej Times, 6 Sep 2026.

questions.q: R. Vairamuthu, who was chosen for the 60th Jnanpith Award (for 2025), writes in which language?
questions.explanation: Poet and lyricist Vairamuthu is the third Tamil writer to win the Jnanpith, after Akilan (1975) and Jayakanthan (2002). The Bharatiya Jnanpith announced the 60th award (for 2025) on 14 March 2026. The award carries Rs 11 lakh, a citation and a bronze statue of Vagdevi. Source: The Federal, 14 Mar 2026.

questions.q: Which institution won the European Parliament's Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought 2026?
questions.explanation: European Parliament President Roberta Metsola announced the award to the International Criminal Court on 22 October 2026. The ICC is based in The Hague. The prize is named after Soviet physicist Andrei Sakharov. Source: Al Jazeera, 22 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Francis Halzen won the Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 for his work on which observatory in Antarctica?
questions.explanation: Belgian-born Francis Halzen won for his work on IceCube, which uses Antarctic ice to detect neutrinos. The prize was announced on 6 October 2026. Each Nobel Prize in 2026 carries 12 million Swedish kronor. Source: AP, 12 Oct 2026.

questions.q: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2026 was awarded to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for work on:
questions.explanation: They won for light-gated ion channels and optogenetics, which uses light and genes to switch neurons on and off. The prize was announced on 5 October 2026. The other three options are the 2023, 2024 and 2025 topics. Source: AP, 12 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Who won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026?
options: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai
questions.explanation: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won for work on asymmetric synthesis of mirror-image molecules, which is used to make many drugs. The prize was announced on 7 October 2026. Source: AP, 12 Oct 2026.

questions.q: At the 72nd National Film Awards, the Best Actor award was shared by Kartik Aaryan ('Chandu Champion') and which other actor?
questions.explanation: Mammootty won for 'Bramayugam'. Yami Gautam won Best Actress for 'Article 370'. Source: News On AIR, 22 Sep 2026.

questions.q: At which place in Gujarat did the President present the 72nd National Film Awards on 22 September 2026?
questions.explanation: President Droupadi Murmu presented the awards near the Statue of Unity at Ekta Nagar in Gujarat's Narmada district, instead of New Delhi. The 72nd National Film Awards, announced on 18 July 2026, honoured films certified in 2024. Source: News On AIR, 22 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which veteran actor was awarded the Padma Vibhushan posthumously in the Padma Awards 2026?
questions.explanation: The 2026 list has 131 awards: 5 Padma Vibhushan, 13 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri. The other Padma Vibhushan awardees are V.S. Achuthanandan (posthumous), K.T. Thomas, N. Rajam and P. Narayanan. Banker Uday Kotak received the Padma Bhushan. Source: Adda247, 25 Jan 2026.

questions.q: Alan Greenspan, who died in June 2026 at the age of 100, was a former chairman of which central bank?
questions.explanation: Greenspan was the 13th Chair of the Federal Reserve, from 1987 to 2006. He succeeded Paul Volcker and was followed by Ben Bernanke. He died on 22 June 2026. Source: Al Jazeera, 22 Jun 2026.

questions.q: Teejan Bai, the Padma Vibhushan awardee who died in July 2026, was a famous performer of which folk art form?
questions.explanation: Teejan Bai performed Pandavani, the Chhattisgarh tradition of telling Mahabharata stories, in the Kapalik style. She died in Raipur on 5 July 2026. Source: The Federal, 6 Jul 2026.

questions.q: Actor Nana Patekar, who died in October 2026, won a National Film Award for his role as the gangster Anna in which 1989 film?
questions.explanation: Nana Patekar died in Goa on 8 October 2026, aged 75. He received the Padma Shri in 2013. His other films include Krantiveer and Welcome. Source: The Federal, 8 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Who was awarded the Ashok Chakra, India's highest peacetime gallantry award, on Republic Day 2026?
questions.explanation: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, who in June 2025 became the first Indian to visit the International Space Station on the Axiom-4 mission, received the Ashok Chakra. Fellow Gaganyaan astronaut-designate Prashanth Balakrishnan Nair received the Kirti Chakra, the second-highest peacetime gallantry award. Source: Adda247, 26 Jan 2026.

questions.q: Sir Garfield Sobers, who died in July 2026, played Test cricket for which team?
questions.explanation: The Barbados-born all-rounder played for the West Indies from 1954 to 1974 and died on 17 July 2026, aged 89. He scored 365 not out against Pakistan in 1958 and hit six sixes in an over in 1968. Source: Adda247, 18 Jul 2026.

questions.q: Who was named the World Food Prize laureate for 2026?
questions.explanation: Dutch food safety scientist Huub Lelieveld is the 2026 laureate, honoured for translating the science of food safety into a global force for action. The prize carries USD 500,000 and is presented in Des Moines, Iowa (USA). The 2025 laureate was Brazil's Mariangela Hungria, and the 2024 laureates were Cary Fowler and Geoffrey Hawtin. Source: World Food Prize Foundation (via Wikipedia), 2026.

questions.q: Which country topped the medal table at the 2026 Commonwealth Games held in Glasgow?
questions.explanation: Australia finished first with 171 medals (70 gold, 45 silver, 56 bronze). England was second with 29 gold and Canada third with 19 gold. The Games were held in Glasgow from 23 July to 2 August 2026. Source: The Week, 2 Aug 2026.

questions.q: How many medals in total did India win at the 20th Asian Games 2026, where it finished fourth?
questions.explanation: India won 85 medals (21 gold, 27 silver, 37 bronze) and finished 4th. Uzbekistan also won 21 gold but had fewer silver medals (25), so it finished 5th. Source: News On AIR, 5 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Which Indian city will host the 2030 Commonwealth Games, the centenary edition of the Games?
questions.explanation: Glasgow handed the Games over to Ahmedabad (Amdavad) at the closing ceremony on 2 August 2026. It will be India's second Commonwealth Games after New Delhi 2010. Source: The Week, 2 Aug 2026.

questions.q: How many medals did Indian boxers win at the Asian Games 2026?
questions.explanation: India won six boxing medals: three gold (Lovlina Borgohain 75 kg, Parveen Hooda 65 kg, Ankush Panghal 80 kg) and three bronze (Priya Ghanghas 60 kg, Kapil Pokhariya 90 kg, Narender Berwal +90 kg). Lovlina had won bronze at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics. Source: News On AIR, 5 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Which country finished first in the medal table of the Asian Games 2026?
questions.explanation: China topped the table with 341 medals, including 169 gold. Host Japan was second (83 gold) and South Korea third (39 gold); India was fourth with 21 gold. Source: Outlook India, Oct 2026.

questions.q: India won 39 medals at the 2026 Commonwealth Games. At which position did it finish in the medal table?
questions.explanation: India finished 4th with 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze. Host Scotland also had 13 gold and 39 medals but fewer silver, so it was 5th. Source: The Week, 2 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Which city received the Olympic Council of Asia flag in October 2026 as host of the next Asian Games in 2030?
questions.explanation: Doha (Qatar) will host the 21st Asian Games in 2030; it last hosted in 2006. Riyadh (Saudi Arabia) will host the 2034 edition. Source: Qatar News Agency, 4 Oct 2026.

questions.q: The 20th Asian Games were held from 19 September to 4 October 2026 in which Japanese host region?
questions.explanation: Aichi Prefecture and its capital Nagoya hosted the 20th Asian Games. Japan had earlier hosted the Games in Tokyo (1958) and Hiroshima (1994). The Games slogan was 'Imagine One Asia'. Source: Olympic Council of Asia.

questions.q: What is the name of the unicorn mascot of the 2026 Commonwealth Games?
questions.explanation: Finnie, a unicorn (Scotland's national animal), was the Glasgow 2026 mascot. Perry was the Birmingham 2022 mascot, Borobi Gold Coast 2018 and Clyde Glasgow 2014. Source: Glasgow 2026 official website.

questions.q: What is the name of the official mascot of the Asian Games 2026?
questions.explanation: Honohon is the mascot of the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games; its design is based on the shachihoko, the mythical tiger-headed fish seen on the roof of Nagoya Castle. Miraitowa was the Tokyo 2020 Olympic mascot, Chenchen one of the Hangzhou Asian Games mascots and Bhin Bhin a Jakarta-Palembang 2018 mascot. Source: Wikipedia (2026 Asian Games), citing the Olympic Council of Asia.

questions.q: Who was India's flag-bearer at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Commonwealth Games on 23 July 2026?
questions.explanation: Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu carried the flag and boxer Lovlina Borgohain was the baton-bearer at the OVO Hydro, Glasgow, where King Charles III opened the 23rd Games. Chanu later won India's first gold of the Games, in the women's 48 kg class. Source: News On AIR, 24 Jul 2026.

questions.q: Which country won the 2026 FIFA World Cup by beating Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final on 19 July 2026?
questions.explanation: Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute at the New York New Jersey (MetLife) Stadium to give Spain its second title after 2010. Rodri won the Golden Ball and France's Kylian Mbappe the Golden Boot with 10 goals. Source: Al Jazeera, 20 Jul 2026.

questions.q: In which sport did India win seven gold medals, its highest from any sport, at the 2026 Commonwealth Games?
questions.explanation: Indian boxers won 10 medals (7 gold, 3 silver), India's best boxing show at a Commonwealth Games. Gold winners included Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Arundhati Choudhary, Sachin Siwach and Ankush Panghal. Source: The Week, 2 Aug 2026.

questions.q: The Indian women's hockey team won its first Asian Games gold since 1982 by beating which country 1-0 in the final in October 2026?
questions.explanation: Lalremsiami scored the only goal against China, giving India its second women's hockey gold at the Asian Games, 44 years after 1982. The men's team beat Malaysia 5-1 to keep its title, and both teams qualified directly for the 2028 Olympics. Source: News On AIR, 5 Oct 2026.

questions.q: India retained the men's cricket gold medal at the Asian Games 2026 by beating which team in the final?
questions.explanation: India beat Pakistan by 19 runs in the final. The Indian women's team also retained its gold, beating Sri Lanka by 147 runs. At Hangzhou 2022 (held in 2023), the men's final against Afghanistan was washed out and India took gold on its higher seeding. Source: News On AIR, 5 Oct 2026.

questions.q: The scaled-down 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow featured how many sports?
questions.explanation: Glasgow 2026 had 10 sports, the fewest at a Commonwealth Games since 1994; hockey, wrestling, shooting, badminton, table tennis and cricket were not on the programme. Teams from all 74 Commonwealth nations and territories took part, from 23 July to 2 August 2026. Source: Wikipedia (2026 Commonwealth Games), Aug 2026.

questions.q: Which team won the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026, beating hosts England in the final at Lord's on 5 July 2026?
questions.explanation: Australia won by seven wickets for a record seventh Women's T20 World Cup title. Beth Mooney was player of the final. Source: ICC, 5 Jul 2026.

questions.q: Which Mercedes driver became the youngest Formula 1 World Champion by sealing the 2026 title at the Mexico City Grand Prix on 1 November 2026?
questions.explanation: Italy's Kimi Antonelli, aged 20, clinched his first title by finishing third in Mexico City; Max Verstappen won the race. Lando Norris was the 2025 champion. Source: Formula1.com, 1 Nov 2026.

questions.q: Who won the men's Ballon d'Or 2026, announced in October 2026?
questions.explanation: England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane won his first Ballon d'Or, ahead of Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal; he also took the Gerd Muller Trophy. Spain's Alexia Putellas won the women's award for the third time. Source: ESPN, Oct 2026.

questions.q: Who won the men's singles title at Wimbledon 2026?
questions.explanation: Italy's Jannik Sinner beat Alexander Zverev in four sets for his second straight Wimbledon title and fifth Grand Slam. Linda Noskova of Czechia won the women's singles. Source: News On AIR, 13 Jul 2026.

questions.q: Who won the men's singles title at the US Open 2026, beating Ben Shelton in the final?
questions.explanation: Germany's Alexander Zverev won in four sets on 13 September 2026 for his second Grand Slam of the year after the French Open. Elena Rybakina beat Aryna Sabalenka for the women's title. Source: Associated Press, 13 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which country won the FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2026, beating Spain 1-0 in the final on 30 August 2026?
questions.explanation: Germany retained the title for its fourth World Cup; the final was at Wavre, Belgium. Belgium and the Netherlands co-hosted, and Argentina won the women's title. Source: News On AIR, 30 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Which of the following Asian Games 2026 gold medallist and sport pairs is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Pranavi Urs won the women's individual golf gold. Aman Sehrawat won gold in wrestling, Parveen Hooda in boxing (65 kg) and Kumkum Mohod in recurve archery. Source: Outlook India, Oct 2026.

questions.q: Which city is the venue of the FIDE World Chess Championship Match 2026 between D. Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov, scheduled from 24 November 2026?
questions.explanation: The match is at the Fondation Martin Bodmer, Cologny, Geneva, Switzerland: opening ceremony on 22 November, first game on 24 November and tie-breaks (if needed) on 12 December 2026, with a prize fund of USD 2.5 million over 14 classical games. D. Gukesh is the defending champion; Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan won the Candidates 2026. The result will not be known before mid-December. Source: FIDE, 14 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Who were India's flag-bearers at the opening ceremony of the Asian Games 2026 on 19 September 2026?
options: Tajinderpal Singh Toor and Mirabai Chanu
questions.explanation: Shooter Manu Bhaker and kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat led India; Sehrawat replaced shot putter Tajinderpal Singh Toor, who was named first. Shooter Neeru Dhanda carried the flag at the closing ceremony. Source: Indian Olympic Association via Adda247, 19 Sep 2026; Wikipedia.

questions.q: Which city hosted the 2026 Summer Youth Olympic Games, the first Olympic event held in Africa?
questions.explanation: Dakar, Senegal, hosted the 4th Summer Youth Olympic Games from 31 October to 13 November 2026. The previous edition was in Buenos Aires in 2018. Source: Wikipedia (2026 Summer Youth Olympics), citing Olympics.com.

questions.q: Which of the following trophy and sport pairs is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: The Thomas Cup is the men's world team badminton championship. The Davis Cup is tennis, the Durand Cup is football and the Ranji Trophy is cricket. Source: BWF.

questions.q: Which of the following sports term and sport pairs is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: A bully is a hockey term: two opposing players tap sticks and then contest the ball, a method traditionally used to start or restart play. Birdie belongs to golf, checkmate to chess and LBW to cricket. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica.

questions.q: Which city will host the 2028 Summer Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Los Angeles hosts the 2028 Games, where cricket returns to the Olympics. Brisbane will host in 2032; Paris hosted in 2024. Source: International Olympic Committee.

questions.q: Which three countries will co-host the 2030 FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation: Morocco, Portugal and Spain will host in 2030, with three centenary matches in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay. Saudi Arabia will host the 2034 World Cup. Source: FIFA, Dec 2024.

questions.q: Which countries will co-host the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027?
questions.explanation: The 2027 ODI World Cup will be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. India and Bangladesh will co-host the 2031 edition. Source: ICC.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of the International Cricket Council (ICC)?
questions.explanation: The ICC moved its headquarters from Lord's, London, to Dubai in 2005. FIFA is based in Zurich, the IOC in Lausanne and the BCCI in Mumbai. Source: ICC.

questions.q: The NVS-03 satellite, launched by ISRO's GSLV-F18 on 30 October 2026, belongs to which satellite system?
questions.explanation: NVS-03 is the third second-generation satellite of NavIC, India's regional navigation system. It flew on GSLV-F18, the 20th GSLV flight, from the Second Launch Pad at Sriharikota, and adds an L1 signal to the L5 and S bands. Source: ISRO, 30 Oct 2026.

questions.q: India's total number of Ramsar sites rose to how many in October 2026?
questions.explanation: India's Ramsar tally reached 103 when Sukhna Wetland (Chandigarh) and Sauj Jheel (Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh) were announced as new sites on 15 October 2026. The 100th site, Surha Tal (Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary) in Ballia, came in June 2026 and the 101st, Glaw Lake in Arunachal Pradesh, in August 2026. India had 26 Ramsar sites in 2014. Source: News On AIR, 16 Oct 2026.

questions.q: What is the full form of NavIC, India's regional satellite navigation system?
questions.explanation: NavIC means Navigation with Indian Constellation; it was earlier called IRNSS (Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System). It covers India and up to 1,500 km beyond its boundary. Source: ISRO.

questions.q: The Ramsar Convention on wetlands, under which India got two more sites in October 2026, was adopted in 1971 in a city of which country?
questions.explanation: The Convention was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran. India became a party on 1 February 1982, and its first sites (1981) were Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park. Source: PIB New India Samachar, 1-15 Jul 2026.

questions.q: Sukhna Lake, which was added to India's list of Ramsar sites in October 2026, is located in:
questions.explanation: Sukhna Wetland, a reservoir created in 1958 at the foot of the Shivalik hills, is Chandigarh's first Ramsar site. It was announced on 15 October 2026 together with Sauj Jheel in Mainpuri district, Uttar Pradesh, taking India's total to 103. Mainpuri is now the only district with two Ramsar sites (the other is Saman Bird Sanctuary). Source: News On AIR, 16 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Which satellite, launched by GSLV-F17 on 4 September 2026, is India's first imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit?
questions.explanation: EOS-05 is an Earth observation satellite and India's first imaging satellite for geosynchronous orbit. GSLV-F17 was the 19th GSLV flight and ISRO's first successful launch of 2026, after PSLV-C62 failed in January. Source: ISRO; The Week, 4 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which company built Vikram-1, which on 18 July 2026 became India's first privately developed rocket to reach orbit?
questions.explanation: Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace launched Vikram-1 from Sriharikota on its 'Aagaman' mission. India became the third country with private orbital launch capability, after the US and China. Source: Space.com, 18 Jul 2026.

questions.q: The joint military exercise 'Yudh Abhyas', whose 22nd edition began on 15 September 2026, is held between India and which country?
questions.explanation: Yudh Abhyas is the India-US army exercise. The 2026 edition was held at Auli (Uttarakhand) and Mahajan Field Firing Range (Rajasthan) with 600 troops from each side. Source: MP-IDSA Defence Newsletter, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which of the following joint military exercises is correctly matched with India's partner country?
questions.explanation: Nomadic Elephant (18th edition, Pithoragarh, September 2026) is with Mongolia. MAITREE is with Thailand, SLINEX is the naval exercise with Sri Lanka, and AUSTRAHIND is with Australia. Source: MP-IDSA Defence Newsletters, Aug-Oct 2026.

questions.q: Pralay, flight-tested by DRDO on 5 November 2026 from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island, is what type of weapon?
questions.explanation: Pralay is an indigenous quasi-ballistic missile developed by Research Centre Imarat, Hyderabad. The test was part of user evaluation trials off the Odisha coast. Source: News On AIR, 5 Nov 2026.

questions.q: INS Samarthak, the Indian Navy's first Multi-Purpose Vessel, commissioned at Karwar on 16 October 2026, was built by:
questions.explanation: INS Samarthak was built by Larsen & Toubro at its Kattupalli shipyard near Chennai and commissioned at Naval Base Karwar in the presence of Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan. It will be used for weapons and sensor trials, maritime surveillance and as a mothership for uncrewed systems; its sister ship is Utkarsh. Source: Open / PTI, 16 Oct 2026.

questions.q: INS Mahendragiri, commissioned into the Indian Navy at Visakhapatnam on 11 July 2026, is a stealth frigate of which project?
questions.explanation: INS Mahendragiri is the sixth of seven Project 17A (Nilgiri-class) frigates and was built by Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders, Mumbai. INS Dunagiri, the fifth, was commissioned in June 2026. Source: MP-IDSA Defence Newsletter, Jul 2026.

questions.q: Glaw Lake, which became India's 101st Ramsar site on 3 August 2026, is the first Ramsar site of which state?
questions.explanation: Glaw Lake is in Lohit district of Arunachal Pradesh, inside Kamlang Tiger Reserve. Source: DD News, 3 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Which wetland became India's 100th Ramsar site in June 2026?
options: Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Tal)
questions.explanation: The Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Tal) is in Ballia district, Uttar Pradesh. Shekha Jheel was the 99th site; Patna Bird Sanctuary and Chhari-Dhand were added in January 2026. Source: PIB New India Samachar, 1-15 Jul 2026.

questions.q: What is the name of the half-humanoid robot that ISRO plans to fly on the first uncrewed Gaganyaan mission (G1)?
questions.explanation: Vyommitra, ISRO's half-humanoid robot, will fly in place of astronauts on G1, the first uncrewed Gaganyaan flight, on the human-rated LVM3 (HLVM3) from Sriharikota. As of 18 November 2026 ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan had G1 scheduled for December 2026; the first crewed flight is targeted for 2027. Source: Business Today, 18 Nov 2026.

questions.q: Who is the Chairman of ISRO, under whom GSLV-F17 and GSLV-F18 were launched in 2026?
questions.explanation: V. Narayanan has headed ISRO since January 2025, succeeding S. Somanath. The ISRO Chairman is also Secretary, Department of Space. Source: The Week, 4 Sep 2026.

questions.q: The Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota, from where GSLV-F18 lifted off on 30 October 2026, is in which state?
questions.explanation: Sriharikota is in Andhra Pradesh and is India's main spaceport; GSLV-F18 used its Second Launch Pad. Source: ISRO; The Week, 4 Sep 2026.

questions.q: The Singapore-India Maritime Bilateral Exercise (SIMBEX), whose 33rd edition was held from 21 to 26 October 2026, took place at:
questions.explanation: SIMBEX-2026 between the Indian Navy and the Republic of Singapore Navy was held at Visakhapatnam. Source: MP-IDSA Defence Newsletter, Oct 2026.

questions.q: Exercise Tarang Shakti 2026, held at Jodhpur from 26 September to 12 October 2026, was hosted by which force?
questions.explanation: Tarang Shakti is the Indian Air Force's multinational air exercise. The 2026 edition, the second after the first in 2024, was held at Air Force Station Jodhpur with the air forces of seven partner countries under the theme 'Power in Partnership'. Source: Adda247, Sep 2026.

questions.q: In October 2026 two cheetahs were released in Nauradehi (Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve), a new home for Project Cheetah. From which country did the first cheetahs of Project Cheetah come in September 2022?
questions.explanation: Eight cheetahs from Namibia were released at Kuno National Park on 17 September 2022. South Africa sent 12 in 2023 and Botswana 9 in February 2026. Nauradehi became the third cheetah site after Kuno and Gandhi Sagar when two cheetahs were moved there from Kuno on 7 October 2026. Source: Free Press Journal, 16 Sep 2026; ThePrint, Oct 2026.

questions.q: Which state has the highest number of tiger reserves in India?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh has 9 of India's 58 tiger reserves; the latest, Madhav (58th), was notified in 2025. Project Tiger was launched in 1973. Source: NTCA list of tiger reserves.

questions.q: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC), which cleared proposals worth about Rs 2.12 lakh crore on 26 October 2026, is chaired by the:
questions.explanation: The DAC is headed by the Defence Minister (Rajnath Singh) and grants Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) for capital purchases. About 82% of the proposals cleared on 26 October 2026 are to be sourced from Indian industry. Source: News On AIR, 26 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Kusha, which DRDO flight-tested for the first time on 23 July 2026, is a:
questions.explanation: Kusha is an indigenous long-range surface-to-air missile meant to hit aircraft, cruise missiles and drones. It was tested from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha. Source: MP-IDSA Defence Newsletter, Jul 2026.

questions.q: Which state has the highest number of Ramsar sites in India?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu has 20 of India's 103 Ramsar sites, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 14. The Sundarban Wetland in West Bengal is the largest site. Source: Wikipedia list of Ramsar sites in India, as of 16 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Cyclone Arnab, which hit the Andhra Pradesh coast near Yanam on 28 October 2026, was named by which country?
questions.explanation: Arnab took a name given by Bangladesh. It was the first cyclonic storm in the North Indian Ocean since Cyclone Ditwah of November 2025. The next name on the list, Murasu (India), went to the cyclone that hit near Ongole on 3 November 2026; Akvan (Iran) comes next. Source: bdnews24 (Bangladesh Meteorological Department), 26-28 Oct 2026; IMD list of cyclone names.

questions.q: Cyclone Murasu made landfall near Ongole in early November 2026. In which state is this?
questions.explanation: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu crossed the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, near Ongole, in the early hours of 3 November 2026, less than a week after Cyclone Arnab hit the same state near Yanam on 28 October. Murasu is a name contributed by India; Arnab was given by Bangladesh. Source: News On AIR (IMD), 3 Nov 2026.

questions.q: The 'Agni-4' ballistic missile was test-fired on 6 August 2026 from the Integrated Test Range at Chandipur. Chandipur is in which state?
questions.explanation: The Integrated Test Range is at Chandipur in Balasore district, Odisha; Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island is nearby. Agni missiles are surface-to-surface ballistic missiles developed by DRDO. Source: MP-IDSA Defence Newsletter, Aug 2026.

questions.q: INS Nipun, commissioned into the Indian Navy at Mumbai on 31 August 2026, is a:
questions.explanation: INS Nipun is the second Diving Support Vessel of the Nistar class, built by Hindustan Shipyard Limited, Visakhapatnam. It is used for deep-sea diving and submarine rescue. Source: MP-IDSA Defence Newsletter, Aug 2026.

questions.q: On 21 June 2026 the Prime Minister commissioned INS Dunagiri, INS Sanshodhak and INS Agray at Kolkata. Which shipyard built all three?
questions.explanation: GRSE built INS Dunagiri (stealth frigate), INS Sanshodhak (large survey vessel) and INS Agray (anti-submarine warfare shallow water craft). Source: MP-IDSA Defence Newsletter, Jun 2026.

questions.q: NISAR, the Earth-observation satellite launched by GSLV-F16 on 30 July 2025, is a joint mission of ISRO and:
questions.explanation: NISAR stands for NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar. It was launched from Sriharikota on GSLV-F16. Source: ISRO launch missions list.

questions.q: The headquarters of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is in:
questions.explanation: ISRO was formed on 15 August 1969 and has its headquarters in Bengaluru. It is part of the Department of Space. Source: ISRO profile page.

questions.q: India took part in CBD COP-17 at Yerevan, Armenia, in October 2026. Where is the Secretariat of the Convention on Biological Diversity located?
questions.explanation: The CBD Secretariat is in Montreal, Canada. The Convention was signed at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit and came into force on 29 December 1993; COP-17 ran from 19 to 30 October 2026. Source: cbd.int.

questions.q: In its World Economic Outlook of October 2026, the IMF projected India's GDP growth for FY2026-27 at:
questions.explanation: The IMF raised India's FY27 forecast to 7.0% from 6.4% (July) and FY28 to 7.0%. The report, 'Resilience Under Strain, Urgent Choices', puts world growth at 3.1% in 2026. Source: IMF / IANS, 13 Oct 2026.

questions.q: What was India's rank among 122 countries in the Global Hunger Index 2026, released in October 2026?
questions.explanation: India ranked 100th of 122 countries with a score of 24.1, in the 'serious' category; it was 102nd of 123 in 2025. India's child wasting rate (19%) is the highest in South Asia. The index is published by Welthungerhilfe and Concern Worldwide. Source: Global Hunger Index (globalhungerindex.org), Oct 2026.

questions.q: Which city ranked first in the Super Swachh League at the Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 awards, presented by the President on 11 November 2026?
questions.explanation: Navi Mumbai ranked first, followed by Surat and Vijayawada. It was the 10th edition, run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and covering 4,751 cities; the awards were given at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. Source: DD India, 12 Nov 2026.

questions.q: What was India's rank among 139 economies in the Global Innovation Index 2026?
questions.explanation: India stayed 38th of 139 economies and leads the lower-middle-income group and Central and Southern Asia. Switzerland is 1st for the 16th year, then Sweden and the USA. Source: WIPO, 29 Sep 2026.

questions.q: In the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 2027, released at COP31 in Antalya in November 2026, India was ranked:
questions.explanation: India slipped five places to 28th (it was 23rd last year and 10th in CCPI 2025). The top three ranks stay vacant, so Denmark at 4th is the best-ranked country. The index is prepared by Germanwatch and NewClimate Institute. Source: Down To Earth, 12 Nov 2026.

questions.q: What was India's rank among 145 countries in the World Economic Forum's Global Gender Gap Index 2026?
questions.explanation: India stayed at 131st of 145, having closed 64.5% of its gender gap. The report was released on 16 September 2026 and is the 20th edition. Source: Daily Pioneer (PTI), 16 Sep 2026.

questions.q: The Global Innovation Index is published by which organisation?
questions.explanation: WIPO, a UN agency based in Geneva, publishes the index; the 2026 edition is the 19th. Switzerland topped it and India was 38th. Source: WIPO, 29 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which country topped the Global Gender Gap Index 2026 for the 17th year in a row?
questions.explanation: Iceland (93% of the gap closed) was first, followed by Finland and Norway. The index is published by the World Economic Forum, based in Geneva. Source: Daily Pioneer (PTI), 16 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Who is India's richest person according to the M3M Hurun India Rich List 2026?
questions.explanation: Gautam Adani and family topped the list with Rs 9.23 lakh crore, ahead of Mukesh Ambani (Rs 8.63 lakh crore) and L. N. Mittal (Rs 3.39 lakh crore). It was the 15th edition. Source: Hurun India, 23 Sep 2026.

questions.q: In the Henley Passport Index of October 2026, the Indian passport was ranked:
questions.explanation: India moved up one place to 84th, with visa-free access to 55 destinations (57 a year earlier). The index ranks 199 passports using IATA data. Source: Business Today, 14 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Which country's passport was ranked the most powerful in the Henley Passport Index of October 2026?
questions.explanation: Singapore is first with visa-free access to 193 destinations. Japan, South Korea and the UAE share second place with 188 each, and Sweden is third. Source: Business Today, 14 Oct 2026.

questions.q: The OECD's Interim Economic Outlook of September 2026 raised India's growth forecast for FY2026-27 to:
questions.explanation: The OECD raised the forecast from 6.3% to 7.1% and projects 6.5% for FY28. The OECD is headquartered in Paris. Source: OECD Interim Report, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which rating agency upgraded India's sovereign rating from 'BBB+' to 'A-' in September 2026?
questions.explanation: JCR, based in Tokyo, upgraded India to A- with a stable outlook on 2 September 2026. Moody's rates India Baa3 and S&P rates it BBB. Source: Japan Credit Rating Agency, 2 Sep 2026.

questions.q: What was India's rank among 180 countries in the World Press Freedom Index 2026?
questions.explanation: India fell to 157th from 151st in 2025. The index is published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), based in Paris. Source: Scroll, 30 Apr 2026.

questions.q: What was India's rank among 163 countries in the Global Peace Index 2026?
questions.explanation: India was ranked 127th with a score of 2.409. Iceland is the most peaceful country, followed by New Zealand and Switzerland; Russia is last. Source: Outlook Traveller, Jun 2026.

questions.q: India got its best-ever rank in the SDG Index of the Sustainable Development Report 2026. What was the rank?
questions.explanation: India rose to 94th from 99th in 2025, with a score of 68.3. Finland is first, then Sweden and Denmark. The report is published by the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN). Source: SDSN, Jun 2026.

questions.q: What was India's rank in the World Economic Forum's Travel and Tourism Development Index 2026?
questions.explanation: India rose to 31st of 110 economies in the 2026 index, up from 39th in the 2024 edition. Japan topped the index, followed by the USA and Spain. The index is published by the World Economic Forum, based in Geneva. Source: WEF; Business Today, 26 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which is the highest-ranked Indian institution in the QS World University Rankings 2027, at 118th place?
questions.explanation: IIT Delhi rose to 118th from 123rd; 52 Indian institutions are ranked. MIT is first in the world. Source: All India Radio News, 18 Jun 2026.

questions.q: The 'Emissions Gap Report', whose 2026 edition was released in October 2026, is published by:
questions.explanation: UNEP, headquartered in Nairobi, publishes the report each year before the COP climate summit; 2026 was the 17th edition. Source: UNEP, Oct 2026.

questions.q: The World Bank, in its South Asia update of October 2026, raised India's growth forecast for FY2026-27 to:
