questions.explanation: The World Bank raised India's FY27 growth forecast to 7.1% from 6.6% in its South Asia Development Update of 6 October 2026, keeping India the fastest-growing major economy. The World Bank is headquartered in Washington, D.C. Source: World Bank / The Edge (Reuters), 6 Oct 2026.

questions.q: In its Asian Development Outlook of September 2026, the Asian Development Bank raised India's FY2026-27 growth forecast to:
questions.explanation: ADB raised India's FY27 growth forecast to 7.0% from 6.6%, citing strong investment demand, resilient services exports and 7.8% growth in the first quarter. It trimmed its FY28 forecast to 7.1% from 7.3%. ADB is headquartered in Manila. Source: ADB Asian Development Outlook, Sep 2026; Free Press Journal, 23 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Who is the author of the autobiography 'Triumph of the Indian Republic: My Life, My Struggles', released in August 2026?
questions.explanation: Former President Ram Nath Kovind, the 14th President (2017-2022), wrote it; it was released on 12 August 2026 at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. Source: Adda247 and AffairsCloud, 12-13 Aug 2026.

questions.q: 'The Second Orbit: Belief of a Man... Dreams of 1.4 Billion Hearts', released in June 2026, is the memoir of which astronaut?
questions.explanation: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla flew on Axiom-4 and is the first Indian to visit the International Space Station. Air Chief Marshal A. P. Singh released the book in New Delhi. Source: Adda247 and AffairsCloud, Jun 2026.

questions.q: 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', a memoir published on 10 November 2026, is written by:
questions.explanation: Sonia Gandhi's memoir is published by HarperCollins India. She became Congress president in 1998. Source: Adda247 and AffairsCloud, 10-12 Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which country topped the World Press Freedom Index 2026 for the tenth year in a row?
questions.explanation: Norway was first, followed by the Netherlands and Estonia. India was 157th of 180. Source: Scroll, 30 Apr 2026.

questions.q: The Global Peace Index is released every year by which body?
questions.explanation: The Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP), based in Sydney, publishes the index; 2026 was its 20th edition. Iceland topped it and India was 127th. Source: Outlook Traveller, Jun 2026.

questions.q: What was India's rank in the World Economic Forum's Energy Transition Index 2026?
questions.explanation: India rose two places to 70th. Sweden topped the index for the third year in a row, followed by Finland and Denmark. Source: Daily Pioneer, 19 Jun 2026.

questions.q: Which is the highest-ranked Indian institution in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2027?
questions.explanation: IISc Bengaluru is India's best at 254th. The University of Oxford is first for the 11th year in a row; 2,297 universities are ranked. Source: The Daily Jagran, 30 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Which economy ranked first in the IMD World Competitiveness Ranking 2026?
questions.explanation: Singapore returned to first place, with Hong Kong second and Switzerland third among 70 economies. IMD is a business school in Lausanne, Switzerland. Source: IMD, Jun 2026.

questions.q: According to the SIPRI Yearbook 2026, about how many nuclear warheads did India have in January 2026?
questions.explanation: SIPRI put India's stockpile at about 190 warheads, up from 180 a year earlier. The world total is 12,187 warheads. SIPRI is based in Stockholm. Source: The Week, 9 Jun 2026.

questions.q: In the latest Human Development Report of the UNDP (2025), what is India's rank among 193 countries on the Human Development Index?
questions.explanation: India is 130th with an HDI value of 0.685, in the 'medium human development' group; Iceland is first. The 2025 report, released on 6 May 2025, had the theme 'A matter of choice: People and possibilities in the age of AI'. UNDP has scheduled its 2026 report for release on 1 December 2026. Source: UNDP (hdr.undp.org), May 2025 and Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which state topped NITI Aayog's first Investment Friendliness Index (IFI) 2026?
questions.explanation: Gujarat was first with a score of 56.6, followed by Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015. Source: NITI Aayog, Jul 2026.

questions.q: At its meeting of 5-7 October 2026, the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee raised the policy repo rate to what level?
questions.explanation: The MPC raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on 7 October 2026. It had stood at 5.25% since December 2025 and was held at the June and August 2026 meetings. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/1264, 7 Oct 2026.

questions.q: After the October 2026 monetary policy, what is the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate?
questions.explanation: The SDF rate is 5.25%, which is 25 basis points below the repo rate of 5.50%. The SDF is the floor of the LAF corridor. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/1264, 7 Oct 2026.

questions.q: After the October 2026 monetary policy, the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate and the Bank Rate both stand at:
questions.explanation: The MSF rate and the Bank Rate are both 5.75%, 25 basis points above the repo rate. The MSF rate is the ceiling of the LAF corridor. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/1264, 7 Oct 2026.

questions.q: In October 2026 the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee changed its policy stance from 'neutral' to:
questions.explanation: The MPC changed the stance to 'calibrated tightening' on 7 October 2026; the stance had been neutral at the June and August 2026 meetings. Dr Nagesh Kumar and Prof. Ram Singh wanted to keep it neutral. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/1264, 7 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Under the Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026, in force from 1 July 2026, what is the maximum compensation the Ombudsman can award for consequential loss?
questions.explanation: RB-IOS 2026 replaced the 2021 scheme on 1 July 2026 and raised the cap from Rs 20 lakh to Rs 30 lakh. A further Rs 3 lakh can be awarded for loss of time, expenses, harassment or mental anguish, and there is no limit on the amount in dispute. Source: RBI FAQ on RB-IOS 2026, 1 Jul 2026.

questions.q: Under the RBI's framework for small-value digital banking frauds, finalised on 24 June 2026, what is the maximum compensation a victim can receive?
questions.explanation: The victim gets 85% of the net loss or Rs 25,000, whichever is lower, for frauds with losses up to Rs 50,000. The amendment directions take effect on 1 January 2027. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/533, 24 Jun 2026.

questions.q: Who is the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India and chairperson of its Monetary Policy Committee?
questions.explanation: Sanjay Malhotra is the 26th Governor of the RBI and took charge on 11 December 2024, succeeding Shaktikanta Das. The Governor is the ex officio chairperson of the MPC. Source: RBI list of Governors, Nov 2026.

questions.q: The one-rupee note in India bears the signature of the:
questions.explanation: The one-rupee note is issued by the Government of India and signed by the Finance Secretary. All other banknotes are issued by the RBI and signed by its Governor. Source: RBI FAQ on Indian Currency, Apr 2025.

questions.q: What is the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) that scheduled banks must maintain, as shown on the RBI website in November 2026?
questions.explanation: The CRR is 3.00% of net demand and time liabilities and was not changed in any 2026 policy. It was cut from 4% to 3% in four steps between September and November 2025. Source: RBI website current rates, 19 Nov 2026.

questions.q: What is the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) for banks, as shown on the RBI website in November 2026?
questions.explanation: The SLR is 18.00% of net demand and time liabilities. Banks hold it in cash, gold and approved government securities. Source: RBI website current rates, 19 Nov 2026.

questions.q: In its October 2026 policy, the RBI projected India's real GDP growth for 2026-27 at:
questions.explanation: The projection was raised to 7.1% from 6.7% in August 2026 and 6.6% in June 2026. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/1264, 7 Oct 2026.

questions.q: In its October 2026 policy, the RBI projected CPI inflation for 2026-27 at:
questions.explanation: The projection was raised to 5.2% from 5.0% in August 2026 and 5.1% in June 2026. Inflation is expected to peak at 6.0% in the October-December quarter. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/1264, 7 Oct 2026.

questions.q: The next meeting of the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee after October 2026 is scheduled for:
questions.explanation: The MPC resolution of 7 October 2026 fixed the next meeting for 2 to 4 December 2026, which is after this exam. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/1264, 7 Oct 2026.

questions.q: From the fortnight beginning 16 October 2026, the RBI raised the minimum daily CRR balance that banks must keep from 90% of the requirement to:
questions.explanation: An RBI circular of 9 October 2026 raised the daily minimum to 99% of the required CRR to tighten liquidity; the CRR itself stayed at 3%. The CRR is maintained under Section 42(1) of the RBI Act, 1934. Source: RBI notification RBI/2026-27/290, 9 Oct 2026.

questions.q: The Government has retained the CPI inflation target of 4% (with a band of 2% to 6%) for the RBI for the five years ending on:
questions.explanation: On 25 March 2026 the Central Government retained the 4% target with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2% for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031. The target is set once in five years under Section 45ZA of the RBI Act. Source: RBI monetary policy overview, Nov 2026.

questions.q: In October 2026 the RBI approved the amalgamation of the Indian branches of which foreign bank with RBL Bank?
questions.explanation: The RBI sanctioned the scheme on 16 October 2026 under Section 44A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. From 1 December 2026 the three Indian branches of Dubai-based Emirates NBD (Mumbai, Chennai, Gurugram) will work as RBL Bank branches. Source: Khaleej Times / Moneylife, Oct 2026.

questions.q: On 25 October 2026 the Prime Minister inaugurated the RBI's new Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in which city?
questions.explanation: The Rs 169 crore facility is at Jatni near Bhubaneswar, Odisha. The Tier IV-certified Data Centre supports RBI-run systems such as RTGS and NEFT, and the institute will train staff in cybersecurity, data science and AI. Source: News On AIR, 25 Oct 2026.

questions.q: In October 2026 the RBI opened a special window to sell US dollars directly to which set of companies?
questions.explanation: From 12 October 2026 the RBI meets the entire daily dollar needs of Indian Oil, HPCL and BPCL through designated banks, until further notice. It was announced with other steps to steady the rupee. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/1306, 10 Oct 2026.

questions.q: The RBI's Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index) for March 2026, released in July 2026, stood at:
questions.explanation: The FI-Index rose to 70.0 in March 2026 from 67.0 in March 2025, led by the Usage sub-index. The index was first published in August 2021 and has three sub-indices: Access, Usage and Quality. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/686, 16 Jul 2026.

questions.q: In August 2026 the RBI said it would resume 'on tap' licensing, stopped for about two decades, of which type of bank?
questions.explanation: The RBI announced this in its Statement on Developmental and Regulatory Policies of 5 August 2026, after a discussion paper of 13 January 2026, and released draft guidelines for public comment the same day. New UCB licences had been paused for about two decades. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/816, 5 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Under RBI rules, an NBFC placed in the Upper Layer stays under enhanced regulation for at least how many years, even if it stops meeting the criteria?
questions.explanation: The RBI's list of 6 August 2026 named 17 Upper Layer NBFCs for 2026-27, including new entrants REC, PFC, IRFC and HUDCO. PNB Housing Finance and Sammaan Capital stay under the norms because of the five-year rule. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/823, 6 Aug 2026.

questions.q: In June 2026 the RBI changed the way it identifies Upper Layer NBFCs to a single asset-size threshold of:
questions.explanation: Amendment directions of 24 June 2026 replaced the scoring method with an asset size of Rs 1 lakh crore and brought government-owned NBFCs into the list. The four layers are Base, Middle, Upper and Top. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/530, 24 Jun 2026.

questions.q: Under the RBI's November 2026 Master Directions on cyber resilience for non-bank Payment System Operators, a cyber incident must be reported to the RBI within how many hours of detection?
questions.explanation: The Master Directions on Cyber Resilience and Digital Payment Security Controls for non-bank PSOs, issued on 5 November 2026, require unusual incidents, including cyber-attacks, to be reported to the RBI within 6 hours of detection. Any cyber security incident must also be reported to CERT-In. The RBI had issued earlier master directions for non-bank PSOs on 30 July 2024. Source: RBI notification RBI/DPSS/2026-27/475, 5 Nov 2026.

questions.q: The RBI's directions that move commercial banks to Expected Credit Loss (ECL) provisioning come into force on:
questions.explanation: The Directions were issued on 27 April 2026 and take effect on 1 April 2027 with a three-stage approach. Small finance banks, payments banks and local area banks are excluded. Source: RBI Directions RBI/DOR/2026-27/398, 27 Apr 2026.

questions.q: What surplus did the RBI transfer to the Central Government for the accounting year 2025-26?
questions.explanation: The RBI transferred a record Rs 2,86,588.46 crore for 2025-26, against Rs 2,68,590 crore for 2024-25. Its balance sheet grew to about Rs 91.97 lakh crore on 31 March 2026. Source: RBI Annual Report 2025-26, 29 May 2026.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India was set up on the recommendation of which commission?
questions.explanation: The RBI was set up on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance). The RBI Act, 1934 gives it its legal basis. Source: RBI, Brief History, Nov 2026.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised on:
questions.explanation: The RBI began as a shareholders' bank and was nationalised on 1 January 1949; it is now fully owned by the Government of India. The Banking Companies Act (now the Banking Regulation Act), 1949 came into force on 16 March 1949. Source: RBI chronology of events, Nov 2026.

questions.q: Who was the first Indian Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.explanation: C. D. Deshmukh became the third Governor and the first Indian to hold the post in August 1943. Sir Osborne Smith was the first Governor (1935-37). Source: RBI list of Governors, Nov 2026.

questions.q: Under the RBI Act, the Central Board of the RBI can have at most how many Deputy Governors?
questions.explanation: The Central Board has the Governor and not more than four Deputy Governors as official directors. The present four are Swaminathan J, Poonam Gupta, S. C. Murmu and Rohit Jain. Source: RBI, About Us, Nov 2026.

questions.q: How many members does the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee have?
questions.explanation: The MPC has six members: three from the RBI, including the Governor as chairperson, and three external members appointed by the Central Government. It is set up under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act and must meet at least four times a year. Source: RBI monetary policy overview, Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which facility's rate forms the floor of the RBI's Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) corridor?
questions.explanation: The SDF, under which the RBI takes overnight deposits without giving collateral, has been the floor of the corridor since April 2022. The MSF rate is the ceiling and the repo rate is in the middle. Source: RBI monetary policy overview, Nov 2026.

questions.q: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) is a wholly owned subsidiary of:
questions.explanation: DICGC is a wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI, formed on 15 July 1978, with its head office in Mumbai. It insures bank deposits up to Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank. Source: DICGC, About Us, Nov 2026.

questions.q: Under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), a resident individual can remit up to how much abroad in a financial year?
questions.explanation: The LRS limit is USD 2,50,000 per financial year, including for minors. The scheme began in February 2004 with a limit of USD 25,000. Source: RBI FAQ on LRS.

questions.q: Up to what amount is each depositor's money in a bank insured by the DICGC?
questions.explanation: Cover is Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank since 4 February 2020 (earlier Rs 1 lakh). DICGC is a wholly owned subsidiary of the RBI. Source: Wikipedia, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: A loan is classified as a non-performing asset (NPA) when interest or principal stays overdue for more than how many days?
questions.explanation: The 90-day norm applies to term loans. Before that the account is a Special Mention Account: SMA-0 (up to 30 days), SMA-1 (31-60) and SMA-2 (61-90). Source: Wikipedia, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: What is the minimum maturity period of a Certificate of Deposit (CD)?
questions.explanation: Banks issue CDs for 7 days to 1 year, in a minimum amount of Rs 5 lakh. Commercial paper also has a maturity of 7 days to 1 year. Source: RBI FAQ, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: How many public sector banks does India have at present, including State Bank of India?
questions.explanation: There are 12 public sector banks after ten banks were merged into four on 1 April 2020. There were 27 in 2017. Source: Wikipedia (Public sector banks in India), Nov 2026.

questions.q: A cheque is valid for how long from the date written on it?
questions.explanation: The RBI cut the validity of cheques, drafts and pay orders from 6 months to 3 months from 1 April 2012. Source: RBI.

questions.q: Bouncing of a cheque for want of funds is an offence under which section of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881?
questions.explanation: Section 138 provides for imprisonment up to 2 years or a fine up to twice the cheque amount, or both. Source: Wikipedia, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a tenor at which Government of India Treasury Bills are issued?
questions.explanation: Treasury bills are issued for 91, 182 and 364 days at a discount and redeemed at face value. Source: RBI FAQ, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: The SARFAESI Act, which lets banks enforce security without going to court, was passed in which year?
questions.explanation: The SARFAESI Act is of 2002. The Recovery of Debts Act that set up Debts Recovery Tribunals is of 1993 and the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code is of 2016. Source: Wikipedia, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: On 19 July 1969, how many commercial banks were nationalised?
questions.explanation: 14 banks were nationalised on 19 July 1969 and 6 more on 15 April 1980. The Imperial Bank became State Bank of India on 1 July 1955. Source: Wikipedia, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) was passed in which year?
questions.explanation: PMLA, 2002 came into force on 1 July 2005. FIU-IND receives cash and suspicious transaction reports under it; the Enforcement Directorate investigates. Source: Wikipedia, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: What is the maximum balance an individual customer can hold in a payments bank at the end of the day?
questions.explanation: The limit was raised from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 2 lakh in April 2021. Payments banks cannot give loans or issue credit cards. Source: Wikipedia, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: How is the share capital of a Regional Rural Bank held by the Centre, the State Government and the sponsor bank?
questions.explanation: RRBs are owned 50% by the Centre, 15% by the State and 35% by the sponsor bank. They began on 2 October 1975; there are 28 RRBs after the 'One State, One RRB' mergers of 1 May 2025. Source: Wikipedia, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: Oriental Bank of Commerce and United Bank of India were merged into which bank on 1 April 2020?
questions.explanation: On 1 April 2020 Syndicate Bank merged into Canara Bank, Andhra Bank and Corporation Bank into Union Bank of India, and Allahabad Bank into Indian Bank. Source: Wikipedia (Public sector banks in India).

questions.q: What does CASA stand for in banking?
questions.explanation: CASA deposits are low-cost funds for a bank, so a high CASA ratio improves its margins. Source: RBI.

questions.q: What does MCLR stand for?
options: Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate
questions.explanation: MCLR replaced the base rate system from 1 April 2016. Since 1 October 2019 new floating-rate retail and MSME loans are linked to an external benchmark such as the repo rate. Source: RBI.

questions.q: Under Basel III norms as applied by the RBI, what minimum CRAR must Indian banks keep, not counting the capital conservation buffer?
questions.explanation: The RBI requires 9% (the Basel minimum is 8%). With the 2.5% capital conservation buffer it becomes 11.5%. CRAR means Capital to Risk-weighted Assets Ratio. Source: RBI.

questions.q: What is the overall priority sector lending target for domestic commercial banks, as a share of Adjusted Net Bank Credit?
questions.explanation: Domestic commercial banks must lend 40% of ANBC to priority sectors, including 18% to agriculture. The target is 75% for regional rural banks and 60% for small finance banks. Source: RBI.

questions.q: Under the Banking Laws (Amendment) Act, 2025, a depositor can name up to how many nominees for a bank deposit account?
questions.explanation: Up to four nominees, simultaneous or successive, are allowed from 1 November 2025. For lockers only successive nomination is allowed. Source: Ministry of Finance, Oct 2025.

questions.q: Which body maintains the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR)?
questions.explanation: CERSAI runs the CKYC registry, which gives each customer a 14-digit KYC identifier. Source: CERSAI.

questions.q: Which authority hears corporate insolvency cases under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016?
questions.explanation: NCLT handles companies and LLPs; the Debts Recovery Tribunal handles individuals and partnership firms. IBBI is the regulator. Source: Wikipedia, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: The capital conservation buffer under Basel III is what percentage of risk-weighted assets?
questions.explanation: The buffer is 2.5% of risk-weighted assets, held as Common Equity Tier 1 capital. The Basel Committee is based at the BIS in Basel, Switzerland. Source: Wikipedia, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: The money market deals in funds and instruments with a maturity of up to how long?
questions.explanation: Money market instruments (call money, T-bills, CP, CD) mature within one year. Longer-term funds are raised in the capital market. Source: RBI FAQ, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: What does LCR stand for under Basel III?
questions.explanation: LCR requires banks to hold high-quality liquid assets to cover net cash outflows for 30 days; the minimum is 100%. Source: Wikipedia, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: NACH, operated by NPCI, is mainly used for which kind of payments?
options: Bulk and repetitive payments such as salaries, pensions and EMIs
questions.explanation: The National Automated Clearing House (NACH) handles bulk, repetitive credits and debits such as salaries, pensions, subsidies, SIPs and EMIs. It replaced ECS and is run by NPCI. Source: NPCI, product description.

questions.q: As per NPCI data, UPI recorded its highest-ever monthly volume in October 2026. How many transactions did it process?
questions.explanation: UPI processed a record 25.47 billion transactions in October 2026, up 23% from a year earlier. September 2026 had 24.07 billion and August 2026 had 24.51 billion. Source: Free Press Journal (NPCI data), 2 Nov 2026.

questions.q: What was the total value of UPI transactions in October 2026, the first month in which the average daily value crossed Rs 1 lakh crore?
questions.explanation: UPI transactions were worth Rs 31.53 lakh crore in October 2026, with an average daily value of about Rs 1.02 lakh crore. September 2026 was Rs 29.37 lakh crore. Source: Free Press Journal (NPCI data), 2 Nov 2026.

questions.q: NPCI's proposed Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on eligible person-to-merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000, deferred in October 2026, is set at what rate?
questions.explanation: NPCI set a 0.4% MDR on eligible person-to-merchant UPI payments above Rs 2,000, due from 15 October 2026, and on 13 October deferred it until after Diwali, with the new date to be announced separately. Payments up to Rs 2,000 and person-to-person transfers stay free, while railways, telecom, insurance and fuel pay a flat Rs 5 on payments above Rs 2,000. Source: Free Press Journal (NPCI data), 2 Nov 2026.

questions.q: Under the RBI's digital fraud compensation framework issued on 24 June 2026, a victim of a small-value digital fraud (loss up to Rs 50,000) gets how much?
options: 50% of the net loss or Rs 20,000, whichever is lower
85% of the net loss or Rs 25,000, whichever is lower
75% of the net loss or Rs 30,000, whichever is lower
questions.explanation: Compensation is 85% of the net loss or Rs 25,000, whichever is lower, once in a lifetime. The framework applies from 1 January 2027 and the fraud must be reported within 5 calendar days. Source: RBI (Responsible Business Conduct Third Amendment Directions), 24 Jun 2026.

questions.q: What is the minimum amount that can be sent through RTGS?
questions.explanation: The RTGS minimum is Rs 2,00,000 with no upper limit. RTGS is run by the RBI and has been available 24x7 since 14 December 2020. Source: RBI FAQ on RTGS, 14 Oct 2026.

questions.q: The IFSC used for NEFT and RTGS transfers has how many characters?
questions.explanation: The IFSC is an 11-character code: the first four letters show the bank, the fifth is zero and the last six show the branch. The MICR code has 9 digits. Source: RBI FAQ on NEFT, 2 Sep 2024.

questions.q: Which number is the national helpline for reporting cyber financial fraud in India?
questions.explanation: 1930 is the national cyber crime helpline, run by the Home Ministry's Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) along with the portal cybercrime.gov.in. 155260 was the earlier fraud helpline number. The RBI-NPCI DigiSaathi helpline for digital payment queries is 14431, and 1947 is the Aadhaar (UIDAI) helpline. Source: Ministry of Home Affairs (I4C); NPCI DigiSaathi page.

questions.q: NPCI was set up in 2008 as an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India and which other body?
options: Institute for Development and Research in Banking Technology
Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.explanation: NPCI was founded in December 2008 by the RBI and the Indian Banks' Association under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. It is headquartered in Mumbai. Source: Wikipedia (NPCI).

questions.q: In August 2026, NPCI International signed a pact so that Indian travellers can pay by UPI through the HUMO payment system. HUMO belongs to which country?
questions.explanation: NIPL signed with Uzbekistan's National Interbank Processing Centre, operator of HUMO, on 30 August 2026 so UPI apps can scan UZQR codes. It is UPI's first entry into Central Asia. Source: Adda247 / Finance Ministry, 1 Sep 2026.

questions.q: The proposed MDR on UPI merchant payments is capped at what amount per transaction?
questions.explanation: The 0.4% MDR is capped at Rs 300 per transaction, a level reached at Rs 75,000 and above. Small merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh a month through UPI QR codes are exempt. The charge was due from 15 October 2026, but NPCI deferred it until after Diwali. Source: ThePrint, 15 Sep 2026; Free Press Journal, 2 Nov 2026.

questions.q: A UTR number for an RTGS transaction has how many characters?
questions.explanation: An RTGS Unique Transaction Reference has 22 characters. A NEFT reference has 16 characters. Source: RBI FAQ on RTGS, 14 Oct 2026.

questions.q: In which year was UPI launched by NPCI?
questions.explanation: UPI was launched in 2016 (pilot on 11 April 2016, public rollout from 25 August 2016) with 21 banks, and completed 10 years in 2026. Source: Adda247, 25 Aug 2026.

questions.q: The RBI regulates payment systems such as UPI, NEFT and RTGS under which Act?
questions.explanation: The Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 empowers the RBI to regulate and supervise payment systems in India. NPCI was set up in 2008 under its provisions as the umbrella organisation for retail payments such as UPI, IMPS and RuPay. Source: RBI (Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007).

questions.q: Since which date has NEFT been available round the clock, 24x7?
questions.explanation: NEFT became 24x7 on 16 December 2019 and settles in half-hourly batches. RTGS became 24x7 on 14 December 2020. Source: Wikipedia (NEFT) / RBI FAQ.

questions.q: NPCI is registered as which type of company?
questions.explanation: NPCI is a not-for-profit company under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013 (earlier Section 25 of the 1956 Act). Its subsidiaries are NIPL, NBBL, NBSL and NTSL. Source: Wikipedia (NPCI).

questions.q: In which year was the RuPay card network launched by NPCI?
questions.explanation: RuPay, India's own card network, was launched on 26 March 2012 and dedicated to the nation in May 2014. IMPS came in 2010 and UPI in 2016. Source: Wikipedia (RuPay).

questions.q: The Bharat Bill Payment System (BBPS) is now known by which name?
questions.explanation: BBPS was renamed Bharat Connect in 2024. It is run by NPCI Bharat BillPay Ltd (NBBL), an NPCI subsidiary. In September 2026 multi-currency forex was added on it. Source: Adda247, 11 Sep 2026.

questions.q: The RBI started the pilot of the retail Digital Rupee (e-Rupee Retail) on which date?
questions.explanation: The retail e-Rupee pilot began on 1 December 2022. The wholesale pilot began on 1 November 2022. The e-Rupee is India's CBDC and is issued by the RBI. Source: Wikipedia (Digital rupee) / RBI, Nov 2022.

questions.q: What is the maximum outstanding balance allowed in a full-KYC prepaid payment instrument (PPI) such as a wallet?
questions.explanation: A full-KYC PPI can hold up to Rs 2,00,000 at any time. A small PPI can hold up to Rs 10,000. Source: RBI FAQ on PPIs, 22 Nov 2022.

questions.q: What is the base period of the RBI's Digital Payments Index (RBI-DPI)?
questions.explanation: RBI-DPI has March 2018 as its base (100) and is published for March and September. It stood at 516.76 for September 2025 (announced 12 February 2026), up from 493.22 for March 2025. Source: RBI press release, 12 Feb 2026.

questions.q: Which was the first country outside India to accept UPI payments through the BHIM app, in July 2021?
questions.explanation: Bhutan accepted BHIM UPI from 13 July 2021 through its Royal Monetary Authority. France (Eiffel Tower) followed in February 2024 as the first in Europe, and Cambodia went live on 2 June 2026. Source: Wikipedia (UPI).

questions.q: UPI Tap & Pay, launched at Global Fintech Fest 2026 in September 2026, works on which technology?
questions.explanation: UPI Tap & Pay uses NFC between the phone and a POS terminal. Payments below Rs 5,000 need no PIN. MyUPI, an AI help platform, was launched alongside. Source: Adda247, 11 Sep 2026.

questions.q: What is the per-transaction limit for IMPS?
questions.explanation: The IMPS limit was raised from Rs 2 lakh to Rs 5 lakh in October 2021. IMPS was launched by NPCI on 22 November 2010 and works 24x7. Source: RBI, Oct 2021 / Wikipedia (IMPS).

questions.q: Which body regulates credit rating agencies in India?
questions.explanation: SEBI regulates credit rating agencies under the SEBI (Credit Rating Agencies) Regulations, 1999. CRISIL, set up in 1987, was India's first rating agency. Source: SEBI regulations list.

questions.q: Mutual funds in India are regulated by which body?
questions.explanation: SEBI regulates mutual funds; its new SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026 took effect on 1 April 2026. AMFI is only the industry association. Source: SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026.

questions.q: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) was set up on the recommendation of which committee?
questions.explanation: The Pherwani Committee (1991) recommended a national stock exchange; NSE was incorporated in 1992 and began trading in 1994. BSE, set up in 1875, is Asia's oldest exchange. Source: Wikipedia (NSE).

questions.q: Who is the Chairman and Managing Director of SIDBI?
questions.explanation: Manoj Mittal is CMD of SIDBI, which was set up on 2 April 1990 and is headquartered in Lucknow. Shaji K. V. heads NABARD. Source: SIDBI website, Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which body recommends Minimum Support Prices (MSP) to the Government?
options: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)
questions.explanation: CACP recommends MSPs and the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approves them. CACP is under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. Source: Wikipedia (CACP).

questions.q: Who is the Chairman of SEBI?
questions.explanation: Tuhin Kanta Pandey has been SEBI Chairman since 1 March 2025, succeeding Madhabi Puri Buch. SEBI is headquartered in Mumbai. Source: SEBI website, Nov 2026.

questions.q: After the 'One State, One RRB' amalgamation effective 1 May 2025, how many Regional Rural Banks does India have?
questions.explanation: The number of RRBs fell from 43 to 28 when 26 RRBs in 10 states and one Union Territory were merged into 11, effective 1 May 2025, under 'One State, One RRB'. This was the fourth phase of RRB consolidation. Source: Finance Ministry / News On AIR, 8 Apr 2025.

questions.q: The Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND) works under which department of the Ministry of Finance?
questions.explanation: FIU-IND, set up on 18 November 2004, is under the Department of Revenue and reports directly to the Economic Intelligence Council headed by the Finance Minister. IRS officer Satya Pal Kumar (2005 batch) was appointed its Director in July 2026. Source: FIU-IND website; Business Standard, 24 Jul 2026.

questions.q: At its board meeting on 24 September 2026, SEBI approved the SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2026. They replace the regulations of which year?
questions.explanation: The 2026 regulations supersede the SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020 and take effect on 1 April 2027. This was SEBI's 215th board meeting, held in Mumbai. Source: SEBI PR 59/2026, 24 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Under SEBI rules, what is the minimum investment a client must make with a portfolio manager (PMS)?
questions.explanation: The minimum is Rs 50 lakh per client, and the SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2026, notified on 7 October 2026 and effective from 1 April 2027, keep it. The new regulations also add a PRIM route for investing in mutual fund units, with a lower Rs 25 lakh minimum. Source: SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2026, 7 Oct 2026.

questions.q: NABARD was set up in 1982 on the recommendation of which committee?
questions.explanation: NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982 under the NABARD Act, 1981, on the recommendation of CRAFICARD headed by B. Sivaraman. Its Chairman is Shaji K. V. Source: NABARD.

questions.q: Who is the Chairman of NABARD?
questions.explanation: Shaji K. V. is NABARD's Chairman. NABARD is headquartered in Mumbai and is wholly owned by the Government of India. Source: NABARD website, Nov 2026.

questions.q: MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency) is a subsidiary of which institution?
questions.explanation: MUDRA is a wholly owned subsidiary of SIDBI, launched on 8 April 2015 to refinance loans to micro units under PM Mudra Yojana. Source: Wikipedia (SIDBI).

questions.q: IRDAI was set up following the recommendations of which committee?
questions.explanation: The R. N. Malhotra Committee (1994) recommended an insurance regulator; IRDA was set up under the IRDA Act, 1999. IRDAI is headquartered in Hyderabad. Its Chairman is Ajay Seth. Source: Wikipedia (IRDAI).

questions.q: Who chairs the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC)?
questions.explanation: The FSDC, set up in December 2010, is chaired by the Union Finance Minister. Its sub-committee is chaired by the RBI Governor. Source: Wikipedia (FSDC).

questions.q: The RBI's list of Upper Layer NBFCs for 2026-27, released in August 2026, has how many NBFCs?
questions.explanation: The RBI's 2026-27 list, released on 6 August 2026, names 17 NBFCs, up from 15 in the 2024-25 list, with REC, PFC, IRFC and HUDCO entering for the first time. PNB Housing Finance and Sammaan Capital also stay in the Upper Layer under the five-year rule. The four layers under scale-based regulation are Base, Middle, Upper and Top. Source: RBI press release, 6 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Which of these currencies is NOT part of the IMF's Special Drawing Rights (SDR) basket?
questions.explanation: The SDR basket has five currencies: US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen and pound sterling. The IMF is headquartered in Washington, D.C. The SDR was created in 1969. Source: IMF factsheet.

questions.q: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) mainly works against which of the following?
questions.explanation: FATF, set up in 1989 by the G7 and based in Paris, sets standards against money laundering and terror financing. FIU-IND is India's financial intelligence unit. Source: Wikipedia (FATF).

questions.q: Which arm of the World Bank Group gives concessional loans to the poorest countries?
questions.explanation: The International Development Association (IDA) is the soft-loan window. The group's five institutions are IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA and ICSID. Source: Wikipedia (IDA).

questions.q: Credit information companies such as TransUnion CIBIL are regulated by which body?
questions.explanation: The RBI regulates credit information companies under the Credit Information Companies (Regulation) Act, 2005. The four CICs are TransUnion CIBIL, Equifax, Experian and CRIF High Mark. Source: Wikipedia (Credit bureau) / RBI.

questions.q: The Financial Services Institutions Bureau (FSIB), reconstituted in October 2026, replaced which earlier body in 2022?
options: Banking Codes and Standards Board of India
questions.explanation: FSIB replaced the Banks Board Bureau (set up in 2016) in 2022 and recommends top appointments in public sector banks, insurers and financial institutions. It is under the Department of Financial Services; S.C.L. Das was named Chairman in October 2026. Source: Adda247, 17 Oct 2026.

questions.q: After its IPO in September 2026, the National Stock Exchange (NSE) listed its own shares on which exchange?
questions.explanation: NSE listed on BSE on 24 September 2026 at Rs 1,800 after an IPO of about Rs 22,560 crore (all offer for sale, issue price Rs 1,785), because an exchange cannot list on itself. Its shares were also permitted to trade on the Metropolitan Stock Exchange from the same day. BSE itself is listed on NSE. Source: Kotak Neo / Angel One, 24 Sep 2026.

questions.q: The SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026, in force from 1 April 2026, replaced the mutual fund regulations of which year?
questions.explanation: The SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996 were repealed by the 2026 regulations. Source: SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026.

questions.q: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) works under which ministry?
questions.explanation: IBBI was set up on 1 October 2016 under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. The Competition Commission of India is under the same ministry. Source: Wikipedia (IBBI).

questions.q: In November 2026 the Union Cabinet extended the Stand-Up India scheme up to which date?
questions.explanation: The Cabinet (11 Nov 2026) extended Stand-Up India for five years to 31 March 2031 with a Rs 4,111 crore credit guarantee corpus, to support 2.5 lakh more women, SC and ST entrepreneurs. The scheme was launched on 5 April 2016. Source: GKToday, 11 Nov 2026.

questions.q: The GOBARdhan scheme approved by the Union Cabinet in August 2026 is India's national unified scheme for which fuel?
questions.explanation: On 6 Aug 2026 the Cabinet approved GOBARdhan as the national unified scheme for compressed biogas with Rs 23,731 crore for 2026-27 to 2035-36. GOBAR stands for Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources. Source: News On AIR, 6 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, post-hospitalisation expenses are covered for how many days?
questions.explanation: PM-JAY covers 3 days of pre-hospitalisation and 15 days of post-hospitalisation expenses, within the Rs 5 lakh per family per year cover. It was launched on 23 September 2018 at Ranchi. Source: Wikipedia (Ayushman Bharat Yojana), Nov 2026.

questions.q: By a decision of September 2026, the monthly wage ceiling for mandatory EPF coverage was raised from Rs 15,000 to what amount?
questions.explanation: Notification S.O. 5109(E) of 17 September 2026 raised the EPFO wage ceiling to Rs 25,000 a month from that date; it had been Rs 15,000 since 1 September 2014. The new ceiling applies to EPF, EPS and EDLI and is expected to bring over 51 lakh more employees under mandatory cover. EPFO works under the Ministry of Labour and Employment. Source: EPFO FAQs on revision of wage ceiling, Sep 2026.

questions.q: According to MoSPI data released on 12 November 2026, what was India's CPI-based retail inflation for October 2026?
questions.explanation: October 2026 CPI inflation was 6.09%, up from 5.54% in September; food inflation was 8.94%. This is above the 6% upper limit of the RBI's 4% +/- 2% target band. Source: Trading Economics / MoSPI, 12 Nov 2026.

questions.q: When the Union Cabinet approved PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana in February 2024 with an outlay of Rs 75,021 crore, it was to be implemented up to which financial year?
questions.explanation: The Cabinet approved the scheme on 29 February 2024 with Rs 75,021 crore, to be implemented till FY 2026-27, for rooftop solar in 1 crore households. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy runs it. Source: PIB (Cabinet decision), 29 Feb 2024.

questions.q: In a GSTIN, which is 15 characters long, what do the ten characters after the two-digit state code represent?
questions.explanation: A GSTIN has 15 characters: 2 digits for the state code, 10 for the PAN, the 13th for the entity number, the 14th is 'Z' by default and the 15th is a check digit. Source: GST portal (gst.gov.in).

questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana, approved by the Cabinet in October 2026, aims to strengthen which institutions?
questions.explanation: PM VGSY (28 Oct 2026) is a centrally sponsored scheme with Rs 7,395.55 crore for 2026-27 to 2030-31, covering over 2.55 lakh panchayats. Central share is Rs 4,869.48 crore. Source: DD News, 28 Oct 2026.

questions.q: In October 2026 the Cabinet renamed the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) as what?
options: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Pension Yojana
questions.explanation: On 14 Oct 2026 the Cabinet continued NSAP for 2026-27 to 2030-31 with Rs 53,428 crore and renamed it. About 3.2 crore people benefit; it is run by the Department of Rural Development. Source: News On AIR, 14 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Which body regulates the National Pension System (NPS), which needs a minimum Tier-I contribution of Rs 1,000 a year?
questions.explanation: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority regulates NPS and Atal Pension Yojana. NPS began on 1 January 2004 for government employees and opened to all citizens on 1 May 2009. Source: Wikipedia, checked Nov 2026.

questions.q: Senior citizens aged 70 and above get how much annual health cover under Ayushman Vay Vandana (AB PM-JAY)?
questions.explanation: Since 29 October 2024 all citizens aged 70 and above get Rs 5 lakh a year regardless of income; families already covered get it as a separate top-up. The National Health Authority implements it. Source: Adda247, 30 Oct 2026.

questions.q: As per NSO data released on 31 August 2026, India's real GDP grew by how much in April-June 2026 (Q1 of 2026-27)?
questions.explanation: Real GDP grew 7.8% in Q1 of 2026-27 as per NSO estimates released on 31 August 2026; the RBI called it higher than expected in its October 2026 policy. The July-September figure is due at the end of November 2026. Source: RBI press release 2026-2027/1264, 7 Oct 2026.

questions.q: In 2026 the Union Cabinet approved continuing PM-KISAN up to 2030-31. How much does an eligible farmer family get per year under it?
questions.explanation: PM-KISAN pays Rs 6,000 a year in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000 by DBT. The continuation for 2026-27 to 2030-31 has an outlay of Rs 3.15 lakh crore. Source: New India Samachar (PIB), 16-31 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Which ministry will administer the unified GOBARdhan scheme (2026-27 to 2035-36) approved in August 2026?
options: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
questions.explanation: The Rs 23,731 crore scheme is administered by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. GOBARdhan began in 2018 under Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation. Source: GKToday, 7 Aug 2026.

questions.q: The Union Budget 2026-27 set the fiscal deficit target for 2026-27 at what percentage of GDP?
questions.explanation: The target is 4.3% of GDP, against 4.4% in the revised estimate for 2025-26. Total expenditure is Rs 53.47 lakh crore and capital expenditure Rs 12.2 lakh crore. Source: PRS Legislative Research, Feb 2026.

questions.q: Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana, approved by the Union Cabinet in 2026 with Rs 5,070 crore, promotes which type of project?
questions.explanation: PM-SSY targets 5,000 MW of floating solar photovoltaic projects with energy storage. PM-KUSUM is for solar pumps and PM Surya Ghar for rooftop solar. Source: New India Samachar (PIB), 16-31 Aug 2026.

questions.q: On 30 September 2026 the CCEA fixed the MSP of wheat for the 2027-28 marketing season at what price per quintal?
questions.explanation: Wheat MSP was raised by Rs 25 from Rs 2,585 to Rs 2,610 a quintal. The CACP recommends MSPs and the CCEA approves them. Source: Business Today, 30 Sep 2026.

questions.q: What is the annual premium for the Rs 2 lakh life cover under Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)?
questions.explanation: PMJJBY costs Rs 436 a year for ages 18 to 50. PMSBY gives Rs 2 lakh accident cover for Rs 20 a year for ages 18 to 70. Both were launched on 9 May 2015. Source: Adda247, 22 Aug 2026.

questions.q: What is the entry age band for joining Atal Pension Yojana (APY)?
questions.explanation: APY is open to ages 18 to 40 and gives a guaranteed pension of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 a month from age 60. PFRDA administers it; income-tax payers cannot join since 1 October 2022. Source: Adda247, 22 Aug 2026.

questions.q: Which body does Article 279A of the Constitution provide for?
questions.explanation: The GST Council was set up under Article 279A, added by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016. The Union Finance Minister chairs it. GST began on 1 July 2017. Source: GST Council website.

questions.q: The Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme (SCSS) pays interest quarterly. What is the maximum amount an individual can deposit in it?
questions.explanation: The SCSS deposit limit was raised from Rs 15 lakh to Rs 30 lakh from 1 April 2023 (Budget 2023-24). The minimum age is 60, the tenure is 5 years (extendable by 3 years) and interest is paid quarterly. Source: National Savings Institute.

questions.q: Who presented the Union Budget 2026-27 in Parliament on 1 February 2026?
questions.explanation: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman presented the Union Budget 2026-27 on Sunday, 1 February 2026. It was her ninth consecutive Budget, and she framed it around three 'kartavyas' (duties). Source: The Pioneer, 1 Feb 2026.

questions.q: After the GST rate rationalisation that took effect on 22 September 2025, what are the two main GST slabs?
questions.explanation: The 12% and 28% slabs were removed, leaving 5% and 18%, with a special 40% rate on luxury and sin goods. This was decided at the 56th GST Council meeting on 3 September 2025. Source: Wikipedia (GST India), Nov 2026.

questions.q: The Income-tax Act, 2025, which replaced the Income-tax Act, 1961, came into force on which date?
questions.explanation: The new Act took effect on 1 April 2026 and uses a single 'tax year'. Budget 2026-27 also cut the MAT rate from 15% to 14%. Source: PRS / Adda247, Feb 2026.

questions.q: State Bank of India came into being on 1 July 1955 by taking over which bank?
questions.explanation: The Imperial Bank of India became the State Bank of India on 1 July 1955 under the State Bank of India Act, 1955. 1 July is observed as SBI's foundation day; SBI is headquartered in Mumbai. Source: Wikipedia (State Bank of India), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Who is the Chairman of State Bank of India as of November 2026?
questions.explanation: C. S. Setty became SBI's 27th Chairman on 28 August 2024, succeeding Dinesh Kumar Khara. SBI's first woman chairperson was Arundhati Bhattacharya (2013). Source: Wikipedia (Challa Sreenivasulu Setty), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: The headquarters of the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) is in which city?
questions.explanation: SIDBI's head office is at 15, Ashok Marg, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. It was set up on 2 April 1990 as the principal financial institution for MSMEs. Source: SIDBI website, read Nov 2026.

questions.q: SEBI, set up as a non-statutory body on 12 April 1988, became a statutory body in which year?
questions.explanation: The SEBI Act, 1992 came into force on 30 January 1992, giving SEBI statutory powers. SEBI's head office is in Mumbai. Source: SEBI (About SEBI), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: The Deposit Insurance Corporation (1962) and the Credit Guarantee Corporation of India (1971) were merged to form DICGC in which year?
questions.explanation: DIC began on 1 January 1962 and CGCI on 14 January 1971; they merged on 15 July 1978 to form DICGC. DICGC is a wholly owned subsidiary of RBI, based in Mumbai. Source: DICGC (About Us), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which of the following organisation-headquarters pairs is correctly matched?
options: Life Insurance Corporation of India - New Delhi
questions.explanation: IFSCA's head office is in GIFT City, Gandhinagar, Gujarat. NHB is in New Delhi, while LIC and DICGC are in Mumbai. Source: IFSCA website, read Nov 2026.

questions.q: The Imperial Bank of India was formed in which year by merging the three Presidency banks?
questions.explanation: The Banks of Bengal, Bombay and Madras were amalgamated on 27 January 1921 to form the Imperial Bank of India. The Bank of Calcutta (later Bank of Bengal) dates from 1806. Source: Wikipedia (Imperial Bank of India), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which bank, set up in 2013, was merged with State Bank of India on 1 April 2017 along with five associate banks?
questions.explanation: Bharatiya Mahila Bank (founded 19 November 2013) and five associate banks merged with SBI on 1 April 2017. The five were State Banks of Bikaner and Jaipur, Hyderabad, Mysore, Patiala and Travancore. Source: Wikipedia (Bharatiya Mahila Bank), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which associate bank was the first to be merged with State Bank of India, in 2008?
questions.explanation: State Bank of Saurashtra merged with SBI on 13 August 2008; State Bank of Indore followed in 2010. The remaining five associates merged on 1 April 2017. Source: Wikipedia (State Bank of India), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: In SBI's digital banking platform 'YONO', what does YONO stand for?
questions.explanation: YONO means 'You Only Need One'. SBI launched it in November 2017. Source: Wikipedia (YONO), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which of the following bank-headquarters pairs is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: UCO Bank (founded 1943) is headquartered in Kolkata. Bank of Maharashtra is in Pune, Canara Bank in Bengaluru and Indian Bank in Chennai. Source: UCO Bank (About Us), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Punjab National Bank opened for business on 12 April 1895 in which city?
questions.explanation: PNB was registered on 19 May 1894 and opened at Anarkali Bazar, Lahore. Lala Lajpat Rai was the first to open an account; its corporate office is now in Dwarka, New Delhi. Source: PNB (Origin of PNB), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which bank, founded in 1911 by Sir Sorabji Pochkhanawala, was the first Indian commercial bank wholly owned and managed by Indians?
questions.explanation: Central Bank of India was established in 1911; Sir Pherozeshah Mehta was its first Chairman. Its head office is in Mumbai. Source: Central Bank of India (About Us), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Prathama Bank, India's first Regional Rural Bank, was set up on 2 October 1975 at which place?
questions.explanation: Prathama Bank was set up at Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, sponsored by Syndicate Bank. RRBs are owned 50% by the Centre, 35% by the sponsor bank and 15% by the state; there are 28 RRBs now. Source: Wikipedia (Regional rural bank), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) works under which department of the Government of India?
questions.explanation: IPPB is wholly owned by the Government of India under the Department of Posts, Ministry of Communications. It is based in New Delhi and was launched nationally on 1 September 2018. Source: Wikipedia (India Post Payments Bank), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: When the Reserve Bank of India began operations on 1 April 1935, its Central Office was first located in which city?
questions.explanation: RBI's Central Office was first set up in Kolkata and moved permanently to Mumbai in 1937. RBI was nationalised in 1949. Source: RBI (About Us), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) was created on which date?
questions.explanation: LIC was created on 1 September 1956 under the LIC Act passed in June 1956, with Rs 5 crore capital from the Government. Its corporate office 'Yogakshema' is in Mumbai; GIC was incorporated on 22 November 1972. Source: LIC (History), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which of the following cities does NOT have an India Government Mint?
questions.explanation: SPMCIL's four mints are at Mumbai, Kolkata, Hyderabad and Noida. Nashik has the Currency Note Press and India Security Press; Dewas has the Bank Note Press and Narmadapuram the Security Paper Mill. Source: SPMCIL website, read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which is the oldest stock exchange in Asia, founded in 1875?
questions.explanation: BSE was founded on 9 July 1875 as the Native Share & Stock Brokers' Association in Mumbai. Its benchmark index is the Sensex; NSE's is the Nifty 50. Source: Wikipedia (BSE Limited), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: How many member countries does the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have?
questions.explanation: The IMF has 191 members; it was conceived at the Bretton Woods Conference in July 1944 and is based in Washington, D.C. The World Bank's IBRD has 189 members. Source: IMF (IMF at a Glance), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Who is the Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?
questions.explanation: Kristalina Georgieva of Bulgaria has been IMF Managing Director since 1 October 2019; her second term began on 1 October 2024. Ajay Banga heads the World Bank and Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala the WTO. Source: IMF (senior officials), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS), established in 1930, is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: BIS is based in Basel, Switzerland, and is owned by 63 central banks. The Basel norms on bank capital are named after the city. Source: BIS (About BIS), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF), set up in 1989, has its headquarters in which city?
questions.explanation: FATF was founded at the G7 Summit in Paris in 1989 and its secretariat is in Paris. India took up the FATF Vice-Presidency for the first time in July 2026. Source: Wikipedia (Financial Action Task Force), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: The World Trade Organization (WTO), established on 1 January 1995, is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The WTO is in Geneva, Switzerland, and has 166 members. Its Director-General is Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala. Source: WTO (What is the WTO), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Pong Dam in Himachal Pradesh is built on which river?
questions.explanation: Pong Dam (Beas Dam) is on the Beas in Kangra district; its reservoir is Maharana Pratap Sagar. Bhakra Dam is on the Sutlej. Source: Wikipedia (Pong Dam), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Wangala, the 'Festival of the Hundred Drums', is a harvest festival of which tribe?
questions.explanation: The Garo tribe, mainly of Meghalaya, celebrates Wangala to thank the sun god Misi Saljong. Source: Wikipedia (Wangala), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: The Godavari, India's second-longest river, rises near Trimbakeshwar in which state?
questions.explanation: The Godavari rises at Brahmagiri near Trimbakeshwar, Nashik district, Maharashtra, and flows 1,465 km to the Bay of Bengal. It is called the Dakshina Ganga. Source: Wikipedia (Godavari River), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which was India's first national park, established in 1936?
questions.explanation: Jim Corbett National Park in Nainital district, Uttarakhand, was set up in 1936 as Hailey National Park. Madhya Pradesh has the most national parks. Source: Wikipedia (Jim Corbett National Park), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which were India's first Ramsar sites, designated in 1981?
options: Chilika Lake and Keoladeo National Park
questions.explanation: Chilika Lake (Odisha) and Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan) were designated on 1 October 1981. The largest Indian Ramsar site is the Sundarban Wetland, West Bengal. Source: Wikipedia (List of Ramsar sites in India), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Tehri Dam, the tallest dam in India, is built on which river?
questions.explanation: Tehri Dam (260.5 m) is on the Bhagirathi in Uttarakhand and is run by THDC India. Source: Wikipedia (Tehri Dam), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: The world's highest railway bridge, opened in June 2025, is built over which river in Jammu and Kashmir?
questions.explanation: The Chenab Rail Bridge in Reasi district stands 359 m above the riverbed on the Jammu-Baramulla line. It was opened on 6 June 2025. Source: Wikipedia (Chenab Rail Bridge), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant, built with Russian collaboration, is in which state?
questions.explanation: Kudankulam is in Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu, and is run by NPCIL with Russian-designed VVER reactors. Kaiga is in Karnataka, Kakrapar in Gujarat and Tarapur in Maharashtra. Source: NPCIL.

questions.q: Sattriya is a classical dance form of which state?
questions.explanation: Sattriya comes from Assam and is attributed to the saint Sankaradeva; Sangeet Natak Akademi recognised it as classical in 2000. Source: Wikipedia (Sattriya), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: The Hornbill Festival, held from 1 to 10 December every year, is celebrated in which state?
questions.explanation: The Hornbill Festival is held at Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima, Nagaland, and is called the 'Festival of Festivals'. It began in 2000. Source: Wikipedia (Hornbill Festival), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Vizhinjam International Seaport, India's first deep-water transshipment port, is in which state?
questions.explanation: Vizhinjam port is in Thiruvananthapuram district, Kerala, and was inaugurated on 2 May 2025. It is operated by an Adani Ports subsidiary. Source: Wikipedia (Vizhinjam International Seaport), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which was the first Indian product to receive a Geographical Indication (GI) tag?
questions.explanation: Darjeeling Tea of West Bengal got India's first GI tag in 2004. The GI Registry is in Chennai. Source: Wikipedia (Darjeeling tea), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Buxa Tiger Reserve, where a tigress was released in October 2026 to start a tiger reintroduction programme, is in which state?
questions.explanation: Buxa Tiger Reserve is in West Bengal and was declared a tiger reserve in 1983. The tigress came from Valmiki Tiger Reserve, Bihar. Source: Drishti IAS, 6 Oct 2026.

questions.q: The Kishau Dam project, for which five states and Delhi signed an agreement on 15 September 2026, is on which river?
questions.explanation: Kishau is a concrete gravity dam planned on the Tons, a tributary of the Yamuna, on the Uttarakhand-Himachal Pradesh border. The signatories were Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana and Delhi; the Centre will bear about 90% of the cost. Source: Drishti IAS, 16 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve, earlier known as Nauradehi Wildlife Sanctuary, is in which state?
questions.explanation: The reserve, which includes the old Nauradehi Wildlife Sanctuary, lies mainly in Sagar and Damoh districts of Madhya Pradesh and was notified in 2023; it is the state's largest tiger reserve. On 7 October 2026 it became Madhya Pradesh's third cheetah habitat after Kuno and Gandhi Sagar. Source: Drishti IAS / ThePrint, 8 Oct 2026.

questions.q: Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve, in Chamoli (with parts of Pithoragarh and Bageshwar) districts of Uttarakhand, was declared in January 1988 and joined UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2004. Nanda Devi National Park (1982) and Valley of Flowers National Park together form a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1988, extended 2005). Source: Lok Sabha answer (eparlib); UNESCO.

questions.q: National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) is observed on 31 October to mark the birth anniversary of which leader?
questions.explanation: 31 October is Sardar Patel's birth anniversary and has been observed as National Unity Day since 2014. Vigilance Awareness Week is held in the week in which this day falls. Source: Wikipedia (National Unity Day), read Nov 2026; CVC circular, 18 Sep 2026.

questions.q: What was the theme of Vigilance Awareness Week 2026, observed from 26 October to 1 November 2026?
options: Say No to Corruption; Commit to the Nation
Culture of Integrity for Nation's Prosperity
questions.explanation: The Central Vigilance Commission set 'Probity for Prosperity' as the 2026 theme (Circular No. 05/09/26). The other options are themes of 2025, 2024 and 2023. Source: CVC circular, 18 Sep 2026.

questions.q: Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) is observed in India on which date?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949; it came into force on 26 January 1950. The day has been observed since 2015. It is also called National Law Day. Source: Wikipedia (Constitution Day), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: India's State Emblem is adapted from the Lion Capital of Ashoka found at which place?
questions.explanation: The Lion Capital was raised at Sarnath around 250 BCE and is kept in the Sarnath museum. The motto below the emblem is 'Satyameva Jayate'. Source: Wikipedia (Sarnath), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution does the President constitute the Finance Commission?
questions.explanation: Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission, which the President constitutes every five years or earlier; the 16th Finance Commission was chaired by Arvind Panagariya. Article 243-I covers State Finance Commissions, Article 112 the Budget, Article 148 the CAG and Article 324 the Election Commission. Source: Constitution of India (Legislative Department), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: World Savings Day (World Thrift Day) was established in 1924 and is observed globally on which date?
questions.explanation: It was established on 31 October 1924 at the first International Savings Bank Congress in Milan, Italy. Source: Wikipedia (World Savings Day), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: What was the theme of World Food Day, observed on 16 October 2026?
options: Water is life, water is food
Hand in Hand for Better Foods and a Better Future
Right to foods for a better life and a better future
questions.explanation: FAO's 2026 theme is 'Innovate today. Nourish tomorrow.' World Food Day marks FAO's founding on 16 October 1945; FAO is based in Rome. Source: FAO World Food Day page, read Nov 2026.

questions.q: United Nations Day is observed every year on which date?
questions.explanation: The UN Charter came into force on 24 October 1945. The UN is headquartered in New York. Source: Wikipedia (United Nations Day), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: National Education Day is observed on 11 November to mark the birth anniversary of whom?
options: Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
questions.explanation: Maulana Azad was India's first Education Minister; the day has been observed since 2008. Teachers' Day (5 September) marks Dr Radhakrishnan's birthday. Source: Wikipedia (National Education Day), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: National Milk Day is observed on 26 November to mark the birth anniversary of whom?
questions.explanation: Dr Verghese Kurien is called the Father of the White Revolution. He was born on 26 November 1921 at Kozhikode. Source: Wikipedia (Verghese Kurien), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Who is the Chief Justice of India as of November 2026?
questions.explanation: Justice Surya Kant became the 53rd CJI on 24 November 2025, succeeding Justice B. R. Gavai. H. J. Kania was the first CJI. Source: Wikipedia (Chief Justice of India), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Who is the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India as of November 2026?
questions.explanation: K. Sanjay Murthy is the 15th CAG, in office since 21 November 2024; the CAG is appointed under Article 148. Gyanesh Kumar is the Chief Election Commissioner. Source: CAG website, read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which of the following has the United Nations declared 2026 to be?
options: International Year of the Woman Farmer
International Year of Quantum Science and Technology
questions.explanation: 2026 is the International Year of the Woman Farmer. Millets was 2023; Cooperatives and Quantum Science were 2025. Source: FAO (IYWF 2026), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Children's Day is celebrated in India on which date?
questions.explanation: 14 November is Jawaharlal Nehru's birth anniversary. World Children's Day is observed on 20 November. Source: Wikipedia (Children's Day, India), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Who was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar was Speaker from 1952 to 1956. Om Birla is the present Speaker; the Speaker is chosen under Article 93. Source: Wikipedia (Speaker of the Lok Sabha), read Nov 2026.

questions.q: Which was India's first satellite, launched in 1975?
questions.explanation: Aryabhata was launched on 19 April 1975 from the Soviet Union. Mangalyaan (2013) was India's first Mars orbiter. Source: Wikipedia (Aryabhata satellite), read Nov 2026.
